title: wo-stage statistiek: data-analyse en weegmethoden
description:
wo- afstudeerstage, start in overleg 

Op zoek naar een statistiekstage?
Analyseer bij het CBS weegmethoden en non-respons met R en draag bij aan betere statistieken voor Nederland. 

Dit is jouw uitdaging 

Het CBS trekt steekproeven onder de Nederlandse bevolking om diverse statistieken te maken. Hierbij is sprake van selectieve non-respons. Om voor deze non-respons te corrigeren, voeren we een zogenaamde weging uit, waarbij personen een gewicht krijgen op basis van hun onder- of oververtegenwoordiging in de respons. Personen met achtergrondkenmerken die ondervertegenwoordigd zijn in de respons, krijgen dan een groter gewicht dan personen met achtergrondkenmerken die oververtegenwoordigd zijn. Zie bijvoorbeeld [1] voor algemene informatie over wegen. 

Bij het uitvoeren van een weging zijn er diverse zaken om rekening mee te houden. Zo kan niet voor alle achtergrondkenmerken worden gecorrigeerd voor scheefheid, omdat de gewichten dan te extreem zouden worden. Daarnaast is het vaak verstandig om überhaupt niet voor te veel achtergrondkenmerken te corrigeren, omdat dit een negatieve invloed heeft op de marges van de schattingen voor de doelvariabelen van een onderzoek. Ook is er een relatie met de doelvariabelen in het onderzoek: op het moment dat er een samenhang is tussen een achtergrondkenmerk en de doelvariabelen van een onderzoek, is het wenselijk om wél voor dat achtergrondkenmerk te corrigeren als dat kenmerk scheef in de respons zit. Het is daarom vaak verstandig om toch zo veel mogelijk te corrigeren voor scheefheid in achtergrondkenmerken. 

Het CBS heeft een reguliere werkwijze voor het opstellen en uitvoeren van wegingen voor reguliere onderzoeken. Een optie die nog niet wordt gebruikt, maar wel interessant lijkt, is het uitvoeren van een zogenaamde voorweging. Hierbij wordt de weging min of meer in twee stappen uitgevoerd, waardoor er mogelijk voor meer en/of andere achtergrondkenmerken gecorrigeerd kan worden. Wellicht is het mogelijk om eerst een correctie uit te voeren voor non-respons en vervolgens een verdere weging uit te voeren die meer focust op de doelvariabelen van het onderzoek en de achtergrondkenmerken die daarmee correleren. Dit soort vragen speelt zowel bij de reguliere steekproeven die bij het CBS worden uitgevoerd als bij potentiële nieuwe toepassingen. In deze stage ga je aan de slag om verschillende opties voor de weging te analyseren, te kijken naar de verschillen tussen deze opties en te bepalen welke keuze de voorkeur heeft. 

Afhankelijk van de resultaten zouden weegmethoden aangepast kunnen worden, met directe impact op de statistieken van het CBS. 

[1] https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/onze-diensten/methoden/statistische-methoden/throughput/throughput/wegen-als-correctie-voor-non-respons 

Dit is jouw stageplek bij CBS Heerlen 

Binnen het team waar je komt te werken, worden nagenoeg alle steekproeven voor het CBS getrokken. Hiermee staan we aan de kern van het waarneemproces en komen er allerlei statistieken langs bij het team. Daarnaast zijn we betrokken bij het maken van schattingen: hoe kunnen we de respondenten op zo’n manier mee laten tellen dat er zinnige resultaten uit onze onderzoeken komen die ook daadwerkelijk iets zeggen over de gehele populatie? 

We zijn een team met hoogopgeleide professionals die hoge kwaliteit nastreven. description:

Dit is jouw uitdaging 

Het CBS trekt steekproeven onder de Nederlandse bevolking om diverse statistieken te maken. Hierbij is sprake van selectieve nonrespons. We ondernemen diverse pogingen om de respons zo gelijkmatig mogelijk te laten zijn (naar diverse achtergrondkenmerken van personen). We proberen daarbij zo veel mogelijk respons binnen te krijgen, maar kijken tegelijkertijd ook naar de samenstelling van de respons. In het bijzonder kijken we daar bij diverse onderzoeken naar in de vorm van doelgroepgericht benaderen [1]. 

Omdat het verzenden van brieven steeds duurder wordt, wordt de afweging tussen kwaliteit en kosten ook voor onderzoeken die alleen via internetwaarneming plaatsvinden steeds relevanter. Bij dit soort onderzoeken worden meerdere brieven verstuurd als personen niet direct de vragenlijst invullen. Omdat deze brieven steeds duurder worden, lijkt het voor de hand te liggen om geen herinneringen te sturen naar personen die nog niet gerespondeerd hebben, maar tegelijkertijd ook tot groepen behoren die al voldoende gerespondeerd hebben. In zekere zin zou dit ook een doelgroepgerichte benadering zijn. 

In deze stage ga jij aan de slag met een van de kernprocessen binnen het CBS: het trekken en uitbaten van de steekproef.
Dit raakt de kern van onze processen: zonder data van goede kwaliteit kunnen we geen hoogwaardige statistieken maken.
Jij gaat kijken naar de gevolgen voor onze statistieken van diverse keuzes die we bij het design kunnen maken. Zijn er verschuivingen in de samenstelling van de respons en zo ja, kunnen we begrijpen waarom die verschuivingen er zijn? En, misschien nog wel belangrijker, is er nog iets te merken van eventuele verschuivingen bij het maken van de statistieken? Wat gebeurt er als je bepaalde groepen weglaat uit de respons? 

Afhankelijk van de uitkomsten is het wellicht handig en wenselijk om een soort doelgroepenbenadering in te voeren bij onderzoeken met alleen CAWI-waarneming. Gezien de stijgende kosten van het versturen van brieven, zou het zomaar kunnen dat we dit daadwerkelijk in gaan voeren.

title: Data Engineer – Healthcare
description:
About PAICON

PAICON is a Heidelberg-based health data intelligence company building the global health data foundation through its PaiX ecosystem, working to close the representation gap in medical data so personalised medicine works for everyone. We harmonise ethically approved, GDPR compliant real-world health data from providers around the world into a global dataset. The data covers multiple modalities on various disease entities. Our flagship product, PaiX Navigator, generates actionable insights for pharma, biotech and AI companies worldwide.

The role

We are looking for a hands-on data engineer to integrate data from our global partners into our platform. Data integration is the core of the role, and agentic AI tooling is part of how we do it. This is an on-site position in our Heidelberg office.

You will work closely with medical, engineering and commercialization colleagues in a small, pragmatic team with short decision paths and direct access to the founders.

What you'll do

- Onboard new data partners, from first assessment of their data through to reliable production ingestion

- Map partner data to our internal data model and work with providers to close gaps

- Build and maintain robust, well-tested data pipelines

- Ensure high standards in data quality and help evolve our database and data infrastructure

- Document data and transformations so that every step is transparent and traceable

- Ensure data is handled securely, de-identified and in line with healthcare data regulations

- Help us apply AI-assisted methods to data integration, with appropriate quality checks

What you bring

- Several years of hands-on data engineering, including building and running production data pipelines

- Strong SQL and relational database design skills

- R and Python skills on Linux systems

- Familiarity with healthcare data standards such as HL7 FHIR and common clinical coding systems

- Understanding of data privacy and security in a regulated environment, including GDPR

- Day-to-day use of AI-assisted development tools and curiosity to go further with them

- A pragmatic mindset: you choose the simplest solution that works

- Ability to turn messy, real-world data into clear findings and next steps

description:
- Permanent position available with a considerable portfolio of works for the next 5+ years 

- To build your career by assisting in the delivery of ‘leading edge’ engineering projects.

About Kirby Group Engineering 
Kirby Group Engineering is an international multi-disciplinary engineering services contractor and leading provider of high-value engineering services to a number of ‘blue chip’ companies. Operating across Ireland, the UK, Europe and South Africa, Kirby has become the engineering service provider of choice in growth segments such as pharmaceuticals, data centres and power transmission and distribution. Our culture is innovative, collaborative and performance focused. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to grow and develop in a company committed to developing talent and rewarding performance.

Role Purpose 
The role of the Senior EHS Advisor is to provide Environment, Health and Safety guidance working with the project team. You will implement and maintain the Kirby management system for the project. The role is to coordinate all EHS Matters within various Project Management Teams and to report constructively all EHS matters to Project Manager. Under the direction of the EHS Manager, the EHS Advisor will be responsible for providing support to the Project Managers, supervisors and workers. This position will provide leadership and coordination of the day-to-day EHS requirements of the assigned project(s).

Key Functions of the Senior EHS Advisor 

- Provide advice, guidance, support and instruction in all EHS matters to management, safety representatives and employees (including where applicable to sub-contractors, suppliers and visitors to sites).

- Provide leadership through good example. Be proactive in all matters concerning the role.

- Identify training needs, report requirements to project team and carry out training as required.

- Audit and inspect projects, agree and prepare achievable corrective and preventive action plans towards compliance to and continual improvement of the EHS on the project.

- Report on business EHS risks, KPIs and trends accurately with data and recommend constructive actions towards continuous improvements.

- Ensure incidents are reported and investigations are carried out in a thorough and professional manner in order to identify root causes and corrective and preventive action plans.

- Ensure that Site EHS Plans, RAMS and other associated site documents are updated and compliant with statutory and other requirements and that they are reviewed on a continuous basis.

EHS Advisor Responsibilities 

- Reports to EHS Manager, Site Managers/Supervisors and Project Manager.

- Is conversant with the contents of the Kirby safety statement, environment manual, risk assessments, aspects & impacts, legislation and procedures.

- Provides advice, guidance, instruction and training in all EHS matters to management, safety representatives and employees (including where applicable to sub-contractors, suppliers and visitors to sites).

- Carries out internal audits and site inspections in conjunction with Site Management, recommends corrective actions, improvements and document findings.

- Prepares in conjunction with site management team a project specific EHS Plan, induction and Risk Assessment Method Statements (RAMS). These shall be compiled and agreed prior to work commencing and ongoing through lookaheads.

- Ensures that the project specific EHS Plan, induction and RAMS are up to date, reviewed periodically and communicated to all relevant persons (including clients, Main Contractor, other contractors, visitors and others who may be affected by that work).

- Visits each new project, sets up the necessary site safety files (Series 500 & 600), registers, abstracts of regulations, posters, SEOR program, etc., and ensures that site establishment complies with the legislation, client regulations and company regulations as a minimum.

- Reviews Contractor Appointments and ensures that correct appointment is carried out and that only competent contractors are used on projects.

- Introduces and implements effective measures aimed at the prevention of incidents at work.

- Reports on incidents and/or dangerous occurrences should they occur to the EHS Manager, Project Manager and Site Managers as required.

- Reports on areas of concern to the relevant party for correction. Persistent and serious areas of concern are to be reported immediately to line management as per (1) above. Retains evidence of communications with relevant parties.

- Carries out incident investigation in conjunction with site management, establishes cause of incident or dangerous occurrence and recommends method for future avoidance.

- Audits the company site safety file, (Series 500 & 600), makes sure that hazards/risks are regularly assessed, that control measures are implemented, that inspections are carried out and that all incidents are reported, investigated and closed out.

- Prepares Monthly KPI Report for their projects, issues monthly return of Site Visit Schedule, SEORs, KPIs, violations to the EHS Manager and the Business Unit Manager. Issues new SDS to EHS Manager.

- Provides training and information to the workforce using appropriate training aids and media as required. Issues records of training to HR to update the training matrix.

- Attends the regional EHS Coordination Meeting.

- Attends the EHS meeting with the Business Unit Manager, as required (1 per region).

- Attends internal and external site meetings as required – safety meetings, coordination meetings etc...

- Implements and promotes the company Incentive Scheme on all projects.

- Arranges distribution and maintenance of fully stocked first aid boxes on site.

- Monitors P.P.E usage and advises site management on type of protective equipment required.

- Issues non-conformances, commendations and disciplinary warnings both written and verbal if required or instructed to do so.

Necessary requirement of the EHS Advisor 

- 5+ Years’ Experience in similar industry. Knowledge of Electrical, Mechanical and CSA preferably.

- Diploma to NFQ 8 in Occupational H&S. Certificate to NFQ 6 Environmental Management. Safe Pass, (CSCS (UK)), Train the Trainer, First Aid, Training Instructor.

- Internal ISO14000 and ISO45000 system auditor.

- Experience with the Construction Regulations and CDM roles, with experience working with sub-contractors.

- Experience with EHS Management Systems, safety schemes and tendering e.g. ISOs, Achilles, SSiPs etc.

- Excellent communication skills, through presentations, reports, written and verbal.

- Ability to work with Kirby / client / main contractor Safety and Project teams.

- Ability to work well within strict deadlines.

- Ability to be able to prepare Audits and EHS reports, to a high standard.

- Up to date with Legislation, Standards, Guidance, Advice and Compliance.

- Proactive in identifying positive and negative acts, ability to follow through with realistic corrective and preventive actions.

- Ability to lead and coordinate incident investigations and utilise root cause analysis.

- IOSH Member or Equivalent.

Why People Choose Us 

Mission that matters. Real impact on small businesses, not abstract metrics

Modern stack. Kotlin/Quarkus, AWS, TypeScript/React/Next.js, and LangGraph for AI-powered features

title: Senior Propulsion Engineer - Combustion Devices (m/f/d)
description:
Mission Brief 

You will be a senior technical contributor within Combustion Devices, responsible for high-fidelity combustion CFD and the physical understanding required to design, assess and mature liquid rocket engine combustion hardware. You will apply reactive-flow simulation, combustion fundamentals and test correlation to injectors, preburners , gas generators, ignition systems and main combustion chambers, ensuring that designs are performant, stable, thermally robust and ready for manufacture and hot-fire testing. 

Your Role in Our Space Mission: 

- Own and execute CFD analyses of reacting flows in liquid rocket engine combustion devices, from model definition and meshing through solution, verification, validation and technical recommendation. 

- Develop and apply premixed , partially premixed and non-premixed combustion models for rocket-relevant propellant systems and operating conditions. 

- Perform steady and transient RANS/URANS and, where justified, scale-resolving simulations such as LES to investigate mixing, ignition, flame stabilisation, combustion efficiency and unsteady heat release. 

- Model injector and chamber flows including atomisation, evaporation, multiphase effects, real-gas behaviour, conjugate heat transfer and wall heat flux where relevant to the design question. 

- Assess combustion stability and operability, including flame dynamics, pressure oscillations, injector coupling, acoustic interaction, chugging and high-frequency instability risks. 

- Build robust CFD workflows in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and Ansys Fluent, including geometry preparation, meshing strategies, solver setup, automation, post-processing and model-quality documentation. 

- Correlate simulations against component, cold-flow and hot-fire test data; quantify model uncertainty and clearly define the limits of predictive confidence. 

- Translate CFD results into practical design decisions for injectors, chambers, preburners, gas generators, igniters, cooling concepts and combustion-device interfaces. 

- Work closely with design, thermal, structures, materials, test, engine systems and manufacturing teams to converge combustion-device designs and resolve multidisciplinary issues. 

- Plan analysis and validation activities, review work from colleagues and external partners, and contribute to technical reviews, development roadmaps and risk-retirement plans. 

- Advance combustion modelling methods, engineering standards and reusable best practices across the Propulsion organisation. 

Qualification Checklist 

- MSc or PhD in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering, computational engineering or a comparable technical discipline. 

- Typically 5–10 years of professional experience in rocket propulsion, with substantial hands-on responsibility for combustion CFD and combustion-device development. 

- Deep knowledge of fundamental combustion physics, chemical kinetics, flame structure, turbulence–chemistry interaction, ignition and extinction phenomena. 

- Demonstrated experience modelling reactive premixed and non-premixed flows under rocket-engine-relevant pressure, temperature and mixture-ratio conditions. 

- Advanced proficiency in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and/or Ansys Fluent for complex reacting-flow simulations; strong capability in meshing, solver selection, convergence assessment and post-processing. 

- Strong understanding of liquid rocket engine combustion devices, particularly injectors, preburners or gas generators, main combustion chambers, igniters and associated thermal environments. 

- Experience with CFD verification and validation, mesh and time-step sensitivity, uncertainty assessment and correlation to experimental or hot-fire data. 

- Proficiency in Python, MATLAB or a comparable language for automation, data reduction and engineering analysis. 

- Strong technical ownership, first-principles judgement, clear communication and professional fluency in English. 

Bonus Skills

- Experience with LES or other scale-resolving methods for combustion dynamics, instability and injector–chamber coupling. 

- Experience with spray combustion, atomisation, evaporation, real-fluid or real-gas thermodynamics, conjugate heat transfer, radiation or reacting multiphase flows. 

- Experience supporting rocket-engine hot-fire campaigns, defining instrumentation needs and diagnosing combustion anomalies from test data. 

- Experience developing custom models, user-defined functions, reduced chemical mechanisms, HPC workflows or automated CFD pipelines.

Our mission is to help democratise space and use it for good in order to improve life on Earth now and for the future generations.

title: Senior Powertrain Test Engineer (All genders)
description:
At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments. 

We believe that true security stems from relentless innovation. By combining elite engineering talent with agile technology and an AI-native operational culture, Stark turns complex defence challenges into field-tested, multi-domain solutions. 

WHY JOIN US 

- The software and systems you work on directly protect personnel and defend European and national sovereignty. 

- You will work alongside industry-leading minds on autonomous systems, advanced propulsion, and secure cyber platforms. 

- We foster a fast-paced, collaborative environment where bold ideas are supported by serious R&D backing. 

ABOUT THE TEAM 

Our team is responsible for designing, optimizing, and validating high-performance electric propulsion systems for cutting-edge autonomous defense platforms. We combine multi-physics modeling, simulation automation, and rigorous empirical test correlation to build state-of-the-art power delivery architecture. As a Powertrain Simulation Engineer, you will work closely with hardware test, firmware, and systems engineering teams to bring next-generation flight platforms from concept to reality. 

YOUR MISSION 

As a Powertrain Simulation Engineer, you will be the driving force behind predicting, optimizing, and validating the performance of our electric Powertrain Systems (propulsion, inverter, battery and cells). You will manage the development and execution of complex 1D multi-physics models to simulate aggressive flight profiles and powertrain behaviors. You will build simulation pipelines, automate data analysis, and conduct virtual testing to guide architectural decisions and validate system capabilities before physical hardware is built. 

WHAT YOU WILL DO AT STARK 

- Design, build, and maintain high-fidelity 1D models of the complete electric powertrain (including batteries, inverters, electric motors, and thermal management systems) using industry-standard tools. 

- Execute standard and custom simulation profiles—including high-power continuous discharge (simulating hover/climb), dynamic pulse loading, and extreme temperature conditions—to evaluate system-level performance and efficiency. 

- Conduct trade studies and sensitivity analyses to optimize powertrain component sizing, gear ratios, voltage levels, and thermal cooling strategies to maximize range and payload. 

- Work closely with the hardware test engineering team (e.g., Dyno and Battery Lab) to correlate 1D simulation results with empirical test data, continuously improving model accuracy and reliability. 

- Provide high-fidelity plant models to the firmware and systems teams to support the development of control algorithms and Software/Hardware-in-the-Loop (SIL/HIL) testing. 

- Develop scripts to automate the execution of complex simulation matrices, post-processing of results, and generation of performance reports. 

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE MISSION 

- Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field. 

- 2+ years of hands-on experience in a simulation, modeling, or systems engineering role, specifically focused on electric powertrains, thermal systems, or battery performance. 

- Extensive experience with 1D multi-physics simulation software (e.g., GT-SUITE, Siemens Amesim, MATLAB/Simulink/Simscape, or Dymola/Modelica). 

- Strong understanding of electric powertrain fundamentals, including thermodynamics, heat transfer, electrochemistry, and electric motor dynamics. 

- Proficiency in scripting languages (e.g., Python, MATLAB) for data analysis and simulation automation, alongside proven ability to interpret physical test data into mathematical models. 

NICE TO HAVE 

- Experience modeling hardware for aerospace, drones, or eVTOL applications, with knowledge of flight physics and high-power mission profiles. 

- Familiarity with 3D CFD/FEA tools (e.g., ANSYS, Star-CCM+) and extracting data from them to inform 1D system models. 

- Experience taking a powertrain component from concept to flight test.

title: Founding Engineer (gn) – Hardware & Bioengineering, Munich
description:
About Cellsor

Cameras digitized vision. Microphones digitized sound. Smell is the one major sense we still can't capture, measure or transmit reliably. Cellsor is building the sensor that changes that. 

We replicate the mammalian olfactory epithelium outside the body – living olfactory tissue on microelectrode arrays – and read it out with machine learning. The result is a sensor that detects chemicals the way a nose does, with the breadth and sensitivity that conventional gas sensors lack. Applications span flavor and fragrance, defense and security, medical diagnostics, food quality and industrial monitoring. 

We are a VC-backed Tufts University spin-out with a working proof of principle and paid industry pilots, with teams in Boston (biology) and Munich (engineering). 

About the role 

As our first engineer in Munich, you develop the instrument that keeps our living sensor tissue alive and samples the air it analyzes. You take it from today's lab setup to a field-ready prototype at a customer site within 18 months. 

What you will do: 

- Define the instrument architecture, then build prototypes across mechanics, fluidics and housing 

- Develop automated media exchange that keeps cells viable for weeks to months 

- Build the air path: sampling, filtration and controlled delivery of odorants to the sensor 

- Integrate sensors, pumps and controllers for monitoring and automation 

- Test and iterate with our Boston biology team 

- Contribute to grant applications 

What you need to succeed 

Must-have: 

- MSc or PhD in mechanical, biomedical or bioengineering, or a related field 

- Built a lab or medical device from concept to working prototype 

- CAD, rapid prototyping, and electronics integration 

- Comfortable with uncertainty: you make progress without a defined path and decide what to build next 

- Hands-on and self-directed – you'd rather test an idea on the bench than discuss it for a week 

- Fluent English; German a plus 

Nice-to-have: 

- Cell culture, perfusion or microfluidics 

- Gas handling or air sampling 

- Startup or grant-funded R&D experience 

Why join Cellsor now 

Cellsor is an early-stage, VC-backed deep-tech startup, funded to focus on building. Most hardware roles mean optimizing one part of an existing product. Here you build the first instrument for a new category of sensor, and your design decisions become the foundation of the platform. The technical risk has moved from "does this work?" to "how do we build it for the field?" – which is exactly where an engineer makes the difference. As the platform grows into electrode integration, machine learning and product design, so does the scope of your role. 

What we offer

title: Agentic Platform Engineer (gn) @ AI Venture, Berlin
description:
This is an Atlantic portfolio venture.

About the Venture 

AI models have moved faster than most companies’ ability to put them to work. The capabilities are there; knowing how to combine them effectively is still catching up.

Frontier labs naturally put their own models first. Companies often follow suit, asking one general-purpose model to handle ten very different jobs. We believe there is far more to unlock in the models that already exist, even before the next generation arrives. That is the opportunity we are building around.

We bring closed providers and open-weight models together behind a single API. Our engine breaks requests into their component parts, routes each to the right model within a cost budget, fine-tunes on customer data and checks the result against agreed quality standards. With no proprietary model to promote, we can choose the right combination for the task.

Lower costs matter because of what they make possible: giving a small team the freedom to build something that would previously have required a much larger one.

Our founder brings considerable drive, a hands-on approach and a strong sense of urgency to building the company. Backed by Atlantic at pre-seed, we are growing the engineering team to bring the product into production, with people already waiting to use it.

About the Role 

As one of our first platform engineers, you will build the foundations that every product feature depends on: the gateway and router, usage and billing systems, customer key management and the European infrastructure underneath.

Much of that platform is still taking shape. Working directly with the founder, CTO and founding AI engineer, you will help turn early architectural decisions into systems that remain reliable as the product grows.

You will take capabilities from design through to production, thinking through their APIs, failure modes, deployment, observability and ongoing operation. In a team this small, building and running the system belong together. You will also work alongside our founding AI engineer on evals, embeddings and open-weight model serving, bringing platform engineering depth to the ML side of the product.

Agentic engineering is central to how we work. You will operate in an agentic way by default, using coding agents as a core part of how you design, build, test and ship software. You'll develop the harnesses and workflows that allow you to delegate and parallelise work effectively, increasing what a small engineering team can deliver. This requires strong coding fundamentals and the judgement to review, challenge and take responsibility for everything that reaches production.

There is a lot to build and an ambitious timeline ahead. We work with intensity, move quickly from decisions to execution and value people who take initiative and see things through.

What You’ll Work On 

Your first area of ownership will depend on your strengths and our priorities. From there, you will contribute across the platform as it develops.

- Gateway and routing: build a consistent API across model providers, with reliable streaming, fallbacks and safe handling of retries and provider errors.

- Agentic engineering workflows: build and refine the harnesses, tooling and workflows that enable coding agents to work effectively across the development lifecycle, from implementation and testing to debugging and deployment.

- Cost optimisation: develop caching, history compression and model selection, measuring savings while keeping estimated costs distinct from actual spend.

- Usage and billing: build accurate accounting for model calls, usage reports, plan entitlements and invoice reconciliation.

- Agent infrastructure and integrations: support tool calls, cost limits, human approvals and runs that can recover safely from interruptions, alongside connectors for services such as Gmail, Slack and calendars.

- Tenancy and secrets: maintain workspace isolation, secure authentication and encrypted customer key management.

- European infrastructure and model serving: build and operate our cloud infrastructure, including the GPU capacity used to serve open-weight models.

- Production reliability: make systems observable, migrations reversible and releases safe, with tests that protect data integrity and logs that keep customer content and secrets private.

The platform will evolve quickly. You will need to move comfortably between improving what exists and learning enough about a new problem to build the next piece well.

Our Stack 

Our backend is built in Python, with a TypeScript frontend in a shared monorepo.

- Backend: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic and LiteLLM.

- Data and queues: Postgres with row-level security and pgvector, Redis and arq.

- Frontend: Next.js , React and TypeScript.

- Cloud and infrastructure: Scaleway, Terraform and Kubernetes for GPU workloads.

- Auth and secrets: Zitadel, Secret Manager and KMS.

- Observability and testing: OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, Sentry, pytest and testcontainers, alongside frontend testing tools.

You should be comfortable with the core backend technologies and ready to learn the rest as the work requires.

About You 

You enjoy the craft of engineering and the responsibility of seeing your work used in production. Faced with an unclear problem, you can identify what matters, make sensible trade-offs and carry a solution through to release without someone planning every step. You naturally look for ways to multiply your output through agentic workflows, rather than approaching every engineering task as something to execute manually.

We are looking for:

- Experience building and operating production systems: several years of backend engineering with real users, typically three to six, and meaningful ownership of what you shipped.

- Strong Python fundamentals: confidence with async code, typing and testing. TypeScript experience is a plus.

- Agentic engineering as a default way of working: you have hands-on experience using coding agents as a core part of your engineering workflow. You know how to break down problems, delegate and parallelise tasks, provide the right context and build effective agentic workflows. Crucially, you have the technical depth to review, debug and take ownership of the resulting code.

- Platform engineering depth: practical experience with Postgres, Redis, queues, networking and Terraform. Kubernetes experience is useful, particularly for our GPU infrastructure.

- Sound engineering judgement: clear APIs, tenant isolation, data integrity, partial failure and safe rollouts. You can explain both your decisions and what you chose to leave out.

- A working understanding of ML systems: familiarity with LLMs, embeddings, evals, model serving and fine-tuning. Experience with LLM APIs, streaming and token costs is a strong plus.

- A disciplined approach to measurement: you benchmark changes, question assumptions and use evidence to understand whether an improvement holds up.

- Initiative and drive: you enjoy getting deep into a problem, finding a way forward and putting in the work to make it happen.

- This is an experienced individual-contributor role, with ownership of the capabilities you build and close collaboration across the founding team.

- Fluent English is required; German is a plus.

Why Join 

At this stage, platform engineering decisions have a direct influence on the product and how quickly the team can build it. You will work close to the founder and CTO, with room to shape the systems you own and see the results of your work first-hand.

The challenge spans AI infrastructure, distributed systems, security and cost efficiency. You will build across those boundaries, take real responsibility early and receive a meaningful equity package in the company you help develop.

We are competing with teams that have more people, more funding and an earlier start. Our approach depends on technical depth, focused decisions and the drive to turn them into working software. We believe agentic engineering can fundamentally change what a small, technically strong team is capable of building, and we're looking for people who want to push that approach forward. For someone who enjoys a demanding build, close collaboration and visible impact, there is a lot to get involved in.

This is a full-time role, based in our Berlin office five days a week, starting as soon as possible.

As Technical Co-Founder, you will lead the development of our AI efficiency engine, working alongside the founder to turn a compelling technical opportunity into a product.

At the heart of the role is a deceptively simple question: how can we make AI models deliver the same or better results at a fraction of the cost? 

You will explore approaches to model routing, fine-tuning, caching and inference optimisation, combining scientific curiosity with the ability to turn promising ideas into measurable improvements.

This is a role for someone who enjoys difficult technical problems, rigorous experimentation and challenging existing approaches. You won't be expected to build every part of the platform yourself. Working alongside our founding AI engineer and backend platform engineer, you will set the technical direction and focus your expertise where it creates the greatest impact.

Agentic engineering is central to how we work. We're looking for someone who already operates this way, using coding agents and developing the workflows and harnesses that allow a small team to move exceptionally quickly without compromising technical quality.

Above all, this is a co-founder role. We're looking for someone who wants to take genuine ownership, work with relentless intensity and help build a company from its earliest stages.

What You'll Work On 

- Drive AI cost efficiency: develop approaches to reducing inference costs through model selection, routing, caching, fine-tuning, quantization and other optimisation techniques.

- Experiment and benchmark: design rigorous evaluations to understand the trade-offs between cost, quality and latency, turning technical insights into measurable improvements.

- Shape the efficiency engine: determine how closed and open-weight models can be combined and optimised to deliver the best outcomes for different tasks.

- Set technical direction: identify promising opportunities, make key architectural decisions and guide the founding engineers in bringing them to production.

- Push agentic engineering forward: use coding agents as a core part of your work and develop the harnesses and workflows that allow a small team to operate with exceptional leverage.

About You 

You bring deep technical curiosity, scientific rigour and an entrepreneurial mindset. You enjoy getting into the details, testing hypotheses and finding approaches others might overlook.

- Strong technical foundations: a solid understanding of modern AI models, rigorous experimentation and the ability to translate research into practical improvements.

- An agentic approach to engineering: you actively use coding agents, know how to orchestrate them effectively and are excited by what small, highly leveraged teams can achieve.

- A co-founder mindset: you're resourceful, ambitious and comfortable with uncertainty. You take initiative, move quickly and want to build something from the ground up.

- Technical leadership potential: you have the judgement to make difficult technical decisions and guide others. Previous CTO or engineering management experience is not required.

We're more interested in exceptional depth in AI efficiency and the ambition to build a company than a conventional CTO background.

Fluent English is required; German is a plus.

Nice to Have 

- Experience with open-weight models, GPU inference or model serving.

- A strong research or open-source track record in AI or machine learning.

- Experience taking AI systems into production or working in an early-stage startup.

Why Join 

With the pre-seed round closed and early momentum behind us, you'll join at a point where there is considerable room to shape what comes next. You'll work alongside the founder, set the technical direction and receive meaningful co-founder equity in the company you help create.

We're competing with teams that have more people, more funding and an earlier start. Our conviction is that exceptional technical depth, focused decisions and an agentic approach to engineering can give a small team a meaningful advantage.

description:
bunch is building the backbone of private markets. We are enabling next-gen fund operations with one integrated system that combines secure data infrastructure, AI-powered workflows and expert fund services. If you value ownership, growth through real responsibility, and working with a thoughtful, ambitious team, this role might be for you.

The Role 

We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager to join bunch’s Reporting team. You’ll own the products and workflows that turn fund and portfolio data into correct, trusted reporting that’s ready to send to investors.

You’ll work at the heart of how fund managers communicate performance and activity to their investors. That means building intuitive reporting experiences and report-generation capabilities customers can trust.

As Senior Product Manager, Reporting Platform, you will:

- Own key parts of our reporting product and its workflows end-to-end

- Make sure the numbers investors see are right, from the data fund managers enter, through the calculations, to the final reports and the LP portal

- Drive product decisions that balance accuracy, compliance and usability

- Partner closely with engineering, design and operations to deliver a system customers can rely on

This role focuses on the Reporting side of the platform. Typical areas include: 

- Portfolio data capture: how fund managers record investments, valuations and portfolio events like follow-ons, conversions and exits, with a strong focus on intuitive UI/UX, data quality and completeness

- The calculation layer between fund accounting and investor reporting: turning the fund’s books and portfolio valuations into correct investor numbers, with checks that tie them together

- Report generation workflows: quarterly and annual packages, capital account statements and PDFs ready to send to investors

- Configuration and customisation: templates, branding, disclosures, and language and currency formatting

- Data readiness and correctness for reports: validation, completeness checks and auditability

- Distribution and delivery: review and approval flows, delivery to investors, and access controls

- Observability for reporting runs: errors, retries, performance and transparency for customers

Top Responsibilities

- Drive roadmap and execution for reporting workflows and the reporting experiences customers see

- Translate domain requirements into clear product specs (inputs → transformations → outputs) with strong edge-case handling

- Partner with engineering to define the right building blocks for scalable report generation (templates, data contracts, versioning)

- Collaborate with design to make complex reporting setup and review flows intuitive and fast

- Work with fund accounting, operations and customer-facing teams to identify friction, ensure correctness and improve time-to-report

- Define and track success metrics across adoption, report quality, operational efficiency and reliability

Elasticsearch powers search, observability, and AI retrieval (RAG) for the world's largest organizations. We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer to lead competitive benchmarking initiatives within the Elasticsearch Performance team. 

You will develop representative workloads, automate reproducible experiments, and investigate how Elasticsearch compares with alternative systems. Your work will identify performance strengths, gaps, and tradeoffs, guide engineering improvements, and help customers make informed technical decisions.

This is a hands-on engineering role focused on building benchmarks and investigating performance, with technical publishing as a shared responsibility alongside engineering and content partners.

A typical investigation might ask how Elasticsearch and an alternative system compare under concurrent ingestion and hybrid search, at comparable retrieval quality and cost, and which engineering changes would improve the outcome. This role offers the opportunity to connect deep performance analysis with product improvements and public technical work.

What You Will Be Doing 

- Own prioritized competitive benchmarking initiatives across search, vector and hybrid retrieval, and analytical and observability workloads.

- Build and maintain automated benchmark harnesses, datasets, query sets, and load profiles that reflect real-world usage, including concurrent ingestion and querying.

- Design fair comparisons with documented system versions, configurations, tuning decisions, resource budgets, and functional differences.

- Evaluate latency distributions, throughput, resource consumption, and cost efficiency. For retrieval workloads, measure performance at comparable recall or relevance targets.

- Adapt and extend workload-appropriate tools such as Elasticsearch Rally, ClickBench, and vector search benchmark frameworks.

- Investigate performance differences using profiling, system metrics, and controlled experiments; collaborate with engineering teams to identify causes and validate improvements.

- Evaluate relevant self-managed and managed cloud deployments, including serverless offerings, accounting for scaling behavior and service constraints.

- Work with engineering and technical content partners to publish reproducible benchmark artifacts and clear technical reports that explain methodology, findings, limitations, and tradeoffs.

- Partner with engineering and product management to prioritize benchmark coverage and translate findings into actionable product improvements.

What You Bring 

- Solid software engineering skills, with experience building maintainable automation and analysis tools in Python or another relevant programming language.

- Hands-on experience evaluating and diagnosing performance in distributed systems, databases, or search infrastructure.

- Depth in at least one relevant area (search, vector retrieval, analytical databases, or observability systems) and the ability to learn unfamiliar systems.

- Experience designing representative datasets and workloads, including query patterns, concurrency, and ingestion behavior.

- Sound experimental judgment, including repeated measurements, variability analysis, warm-up and cache effects, and the distinction between meaningful changes and measurement noise.

- Experience building reproducible test environments and documenting configurations, procedures, and results.

- Clear technical writing and communication skills, with the ability to explain complex findings and their limitations.

- Solid collaboration skills and the ability to turn performance evidence into applicable engineering recommendations.

Bonus Points

- Experience with Elasticsearch, Lucene, Rally, ClickBench, or vector search benchmark frameworks.

- Experience measuring retrieval quality alongside latency, throughput, and resource usage.

- Familiarity with cloud performance and cost analysis, including autoscaling and serverless systems.

- Public technical writing, open-source contributions, or published benchmark studies.

description:
About SandboxAQ 

SandboxAQ is a high-growth company delivering AI solutions that address some of the world's greatest challenges. The company’s Large Quantitative Models (LQMs) power advances in life sciences, financial services, navigation, cybersecurity, and other sectors.

We are a global team that is tech-focused and includes experts in AI, chemistry, cybersecurity, physics, mathematics, medicine, engineering, and other specialties. The company emerged from Alphabet Inc. as an independent, growth capital-backed company in 2022, funded by leading investors and supported by a braintrust of industry leaders.

At SandboxAQ, we’ve cultivated an environment that encourages creativity, collaboration, and impact. By investing deeply in our people, we’re building a thriving, global workforce poised to tackle the world's epic challenges. Join us to advance your career in pursuit of an inspiring mission, in a community of like-minded people who value entrepreneurialism, ownership, and transformative impact.

The Opportunity 

The SandboxAQ AI team is looking for a hands-on Manager, AI Engineering to help us build the future of agentic collaboration, trust and ROI. Our goal is to make agents work well on their own, in teams, and with humans. This includes the following aspects:

- Security : Discovery of agents, evaluation, red teaming, monitoring, guardrails, etc.

- Quality : Measuring ROI of agents and suggesting improvements

- Collaboration : Bringing humans and agents together into one place with shared context

A successful candidate thrives at the intersection of AI and software engineering. You deeply understand how models and agents work, how they can fail, how they can be protected and improved. You have hands-on experience with agents in production, know what works and what doesn’t, know the latest trends and you’re opinionated about the future. You know what you don’t know and enjoy learning to close those gaps. You’ll turn your insights and innovation into real world features baked into our platform - shipping code to production.

This is a hands-on leadership role where you’ll break things, fix them and then harden them for good while also leading a small team of engineers. At the same time, you’ll have freedom to explore, collaborate, publish, and deploy, shaping the field of agentic collaboration and trust from all angles. You will help set technical direction, raise the quality bar, mentor team members, and ensure that the team moves quickly from research insight to real-world product impact.

We’re looking for somebody with the curiosity of a researcher, the rigor of an engineer, and the creativity of a hacker. You will be part of a diverse team consisting of ML experts, security experts, mathematicians, and software engineers, each playing a key role in efficient and effective enablement of the cutting-edge technologies being developed at SandboxAQ.

Key Responsibilities 

- Lead and grow a small, highly technical team while remaining deeply involved in hands-on engineering and research.

- Set technical direction, break down ambiguous problems, establish practical plans for fast, high-quality execution, and build a culture of ownership, low-ego collaboration, thoughtful experimentation, and high standards.

- Create new agentic capabilities, including frameworks for monitoring, guardrailing, and evaluating agents, while staying current on the latest agentic developments and identifying new opportunities.

- Perform classical ML tasks, including exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, and model fine-tuning, and rapidly iterate on prototypes and features based on feedback and evolving product needs.

- Work closely with Product and Research to translate AI research into applicable features and software engineering projects.

- Contribute production-ready code and technical designs, working across engineering to deliver scalable, reliable software.

Essential Skills & Experience 

- BSc in Computer Science or related field with exposure to AI/ML.

- Deep expertise in AI/ML, software engineering, or AI security.

- Strong programming skills in Python, and relevant ML and/or agentic frameworks.

- Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally and collaboratively with a high degree of end-to-end ownership, delivering real world outcomes.

- Ability to pick up other programming languages and technologies as required to ship scalable and reliable software.

Highly Desired Skills & Experience 

- PhD in Computer Science or related field with focus on AI/ML or similar.

- Hands-on experience with at least one of the following: agent orchestration, agent harnesses, agent teams, jailbreaking / prompt injection, red teaming, data poisoning or evasion attacks, secure model deployment or sandboxing, detection and monitoring for AI misuse.

- Experience contributing to open source projects.

- Experience in a fast-paced startup environment.

- Experience in cybersecurity is a plus, but not essential.

We offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and life outside of work.

- Career Defining Work : Your work will directly accelerate the discovery of better drugs and better materials, advance human health, and enable safer and more sustainable technologies by helping customers put AI Simulation capabilities into real world use.

- Compensation: Competitive base salary, performance-based incentives or bonuses (where applicable), and equity participation.

- Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents with generous employer premium contributions, retirement savings with company matching, paid parental leave, and inclusive family-building benefits.

- Work-Life Balance: Fully remote, Flexible paid time off, company-wide seasonal breaks, and support for flexible work arrangements that enable sustainable performance.

- Data-driven mindset, a bias for rapid decision-making, favouring excellence over perfection.

- Proficiency in Excel, including the ability to create and manage complex financial models.

- Demonstrated use of AI tools in analytical work - accelerating analysis, stress-testing assumptions, automating repetitive processes - and the judgment to know when human input is still essential.

- Strong knowledge of financial statements, accounting principles, and investment analysis.

- Capability to comprehend and collaborate with various lines of business.

- Willingness to stretch beyond your comfort zone and embrace new challenges.

- Openness to feedback, with a commitment to continuous improvement, development, and innovation.

- Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, or a quantitative field.

What we offer 

- Receive competitive compensation and equity ownership in Perk

- Rest and recharge with 25 days of annual leave plus bank holidays

- Take control of your physical health with private medical cover and voluntary dental insurance from Bupa, and discounted gym memberships with GymFlex

- Plan for your future with our qualifying earnings company pension plan with Aviva

- Know that your loved ones are protected financially through your Life Insurance if the worst were to happen

- Rest assured that you’re covered by income protection in case you experience a long-term sickness or absence

- Leverage tax-efficient cycle and electric car schemes with Cycle2Work & Octopus

- Join our unforgettable Perk events, including our spectacular annual summer party

- Always feel supported with Spring Health, our market-leading wellbeing partner, providing fast, comprehensive access to 12x therapy and 12x coaching sessions for you and your loved ones

- Focus on your family with 12-16 weeks’ paid parental leave

- Contribute to your community with 16 paid hours per year to spend volunteering for your dearest charitable causes

- Broaden your horizons with up to 20 "Work from Anywhere" days per year

- Stay savvy with access to a wide variety of discounts and rewards

- Follow your passions and take a four-week, fully paid sabbatical once you reach 5 years

AI at Perk

title: Account Executive
description:
We're looking for an Account Executive to close new-logo business for Cytix in a market where most of the people you're calling haven't heard of us yet. 
You'll be selling a product, not a service, into CISOs, security engineers and AppSec leads, which means the pitch has to work on its own merits rather than on brand recognition. This is a full-cycle closing role: you'll run discovery, demo and negotiation yourself, with support from the CRO on the harder deals while you build that muscle.

You'll carry mid-market opportunities to start, working alongside SDR-sourced pipeline as well as your own prospecting, with a clear path to Senior Account Executive as your quota, deal complexity and independence grow.

What you'll do 

- Run full-cycle new-logo opportunities from qualified meeting through discovery, demo and close, sourced by SDR, Marketing and your own prospecting.

- Generate some of your own pipeline alongside SDR support, prospecting into a clearly defined ideal customer profile.

- Run structured discovery calls solo, identifying pain and priorities for your primary buyer.

- Close mid-market deals with negotiation support from the CRO as you build experience with more complex procurement.

- Maintain your own weekly pipeline and forecast, developing commit accuracy over time.

- Work SDR and Customer Success handoffs as directed, keeping CRM records clean and up to date.

What you'll bring 

- 3–5 years' full-cycle closing experience in B2B SaaS, or a strong track record in an adjacent commercial role (for example SDR) ready to step up.

- A track record at or near 100% of quota (around £500k–£750k) in at least one of the last two years.

- Real consultative selling instinct: you'd rather understand a prospect's problem than run a script at them.

- Comfortable prospecting and selling into accounts with little existing awareness of Cytix, energised by the challenge of a cold or lightly-worked start.

- Visible drive and competitiveness, and a willingness to take on unfamiliar deal types or buyer personas when asked.

- Genuinely bright and inquisitive : good follow-up questions come naturally to you, and you're genuinely curious about the product and the security market, including how software gets built and secured.

- Drawn to a business where new challenges show up daily; you want to take ownership of them and lean in, rather than needing everything mapped out in advance.

- Comfortable taking yourself out of your comfort zone when a deal or a buyer is unfamiliar territory.

What you'll get 

- Time off that works for you: Unlimited holiday policy, including a guaranteed 33 days plus your birthday off

- Flexible hybrid working: Work in a way that helps you do your best work, while staying connected with the team.

- A stake in what we’re building: Eligible employees can participate in our EMI share option scheme.

- Healthcare that goes further: After one year’s service, access private healthcare through Vitality, including dental, optical, hearing and therapy cover.

- More ways to get around: Access our company car salary-sacrifice scheme.

- Support for growing families: Enhanced maternity and paternity leave.

About Cytix 

Software never stops changing. Teams ship new code every day, through tickets, pull requests, releases, and increasingly with AI in the mix, but the way security keeps up with all that change hasn't really moved on.

That's the problem we're solving. Cytix helps organisations understand which software changes actually matter, what should happen next, and how to prove the right call was made. Security understood, in other words.

We're a small team with big plans, so every person we hire genuinely shapes what Cytix becomes. That's why we're upfront about our five values: we interview for all of them, and they matter to us more than a perfect CV. They're things you do, not things you are, so have a read and see if they sound like you.

Make the first move . When the goal is clear but the path isn't, you get moving rather than waiting for perfect instructions. If you're blocked, you make a sensible call, say what you're assuming, and explain how you'd course-correct. We'd rather you act and be slightly wrong than sit still.

Find the smarter path. You ask why before how. You dig into what the real problem is instead of just building what the spec says, and you're happy to question 'that's how it's always been done' when the reason behind it has gone stale.

See it through. When something's yours, it lands. No loose ends, no surprises for whoever picks it up next. You keep people posted when things change, and if something falls between roles, you catch it.

Raise the bar. You do the best job possible in the time you've got, whether that's a day or a month. Sometimes that means deep craft; sometimes the smartest move is quick and scrappy. It's about good judgement, and we hold each other to it without blame or politics.

Play to win. You care about the mission but don't take yourself too seriously. You say 'I' when things go wrong and 'we' when they go right, trust teammates to do things their own way, and bring a bit of humour when the pressure's on.

title: ML Platform Engineer
description:
About us 

Bleu Robotics is an AI company developing universal AI software for the deployment of advanced robots , humanoids, mobile manipulators, and industrial arms, in real factories. The convergence of humanoid robotics and modern AI is one of the most significant technical opportunities of the decade, and most of the work today still happens in research settings. We are building the software layer required to bring it into operational use.

We have a strong ambition to become the next Microsoft to run on every industrial humanoid. We have closed our pre-seed round with Top-tier fund to deploy our robot in Tier 1 manufacturing facilities.

We are looking for deeply passionate scientists who can help us push the frontier and build a major lab in physical AI.

Our vision 

To enable a robot to learn a new industrial task from a few demonstrations and operate autonomously, with under one hour between the start of the demonstration and the start of deployment. 

This objective shapes our roadmap and every technical decision we make.

THE ROLE 

We are hiring an ML Platform Engineer to put our robot learning stack in the cloud and own the full stack. The platform will let customers run our learning pipelines on their own data as a hosted service; its exact scope will evolve with the product.

You will be the first engineer at Bleu Robotics with cloud expertise. The scope covers infrastructure, training and inference services, the web front end, security, and cost. The choice of cloud provider and web framework is open; you will make it with the team.

The role is based in Paris and is on-site. 

BACKGROUND 

We are equally interested in two kinds of background:

- software or ML platform engineer who has built and operated a cloud service that runs training or inference jobs on data uploaded by users (e.g., an ML platform team, an MLOps product, a SaaS that runs compute on customer data).

- backend or full-stack engineer with solid DevOps experience who has shipped a web product on a major cloud provider and wants to work on robot learning.

Experience with robotics or robot learning is appreciated but not required. You will learn the learning stack from the team; the team will learn cloud practices from you.

RESPONSIBILITIES 

- Design the architecture of the platform and select the cloud provider, orchestration layer, and web stack, in agreement with the team

- Package our training and inference pipelines (Python, PyTorch) as cloud services: job scheduling, GPU provisioning, artifact storage, versioning of datasets and policies

- Build the web application through which users upload data, follow training runs, and download policies, including its front end and API

- Add interactive, browser-based components to the platform, including simulation, as the product evolves

- Set up infrastructure as code, CI/CD, monitoring, logging, and alerting for the platform

- Implement authentication, per-customer isolation, and data protection for confidential industrial data

- Control cloud costs: GPU usage, storage, and idle resources

- Bring cloud and DevOps practices to the rest of the engineering team through documentation, reviews, and training

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

- Master’s degree or PhD in computer science or a related field, followed by 2 to 3 years of professional experience building and operating a comparable cloud service

- Hands-on experience running production workloads on at least one major cloud provider (AWS, GCP, Azure, or a European provider such as Scaleway or OVHcloud)

- Proficiency with containers and orchestration (Docker and Kubernetes or a managed equivalent) and with infrastructure as code (Terraform or similar)

- Strong Python development skills for backend services, including asynchronous job execution

- Front-end development experience with a modern web framework (React, Vue, Svelte, or similar), sufficient to ship the user-facing application yourself

- Experience with CI/CD, monitoring, and security practices for a multi-tenant service

- Comfortable working in Linux environments with Git

- Professional proficiency in English, the official language of the team. Proficiency in French is not required; many of our employees do not speak French.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

The strongest candidates will combine cloud fluency with experience across several of the following:

- ML infrastructure: training job orchestration, GPU scheduling, experiment tracking, model registries

- PyTorch and the Python machine learning ecosystem

- Physics simulation (MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, or similar) and 3D rendering in the browser (WebGL, three.js)

- Streaming interactive content to the browser (WebRTC or similar)

- Data engineering for large volumes of video and time-series data

- Security and compliance requirements of industrial customers: data residency, access control, audit logs

- Cost optimization of GPU workloads

- An early-stage startup, or a leading research lab (academic or industrial)

THE TEAM 

The engineering team is a dozen top engineers and researchers in robotics and machine learning, organized around three focus areas: Integration, Vision & Perception, and Robot Learning. This position is the first cloud and platform role at Bleu Robotics. You will work with the whole team and with the founders on product decisions. Early hires help shape engineering practices, hiring, and culture.

What we offer 

- A clear, ambitious research mission with measurable real-world impact

- A diverse fleet of advanced robots, including humanoids, on which to run your research

- Research that ships: your algorithms run on real machines in real factories

- Tight collaboration with engineering teams that take your work to production

- Significant ownership of the research agenda as an early member of the team

- A focused, technically strong team and a serious engineering culture

- English-speaking working environment, no French required

- Fair compensation + equity

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
About the Role 

We’re looking for a top-tier Forward Deployed Engineer to join Linkup and work hand-in-hand with our founders, customers, and partners. You'll be part of the founding FDE team at Linkup 

Your mission: help leading AI companies, developers, and enterprises integrate Linkup’s AI-ready search APIs into their products - and shape how the next generation of AI agents connects to the web.

This is a highly cross-functional role. You’ll operate at the intersection of engineering, GTM, and customer success , turning technical integrations into insights that drive our product roadmap, marketing narratives, and outbound strategy.

You’ll be the connective bridge between what customers build with Linkup and how we tell that story to the world.

What You’ll Do 

- Work directly with customers and partners to design, prototype, and deploy integrations of Linkup’s APIs into real-world agentic systems.

- Participate in pre-sales efforts - technical discovery, proof-of-concept design, demo environments.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with backend, ML, and product teams to ensure performance and reliability at scale.

- Partner with the GTM Engineer and DevRel team to turn customer learnings into automation, tutorials, and playbooks.

- Identify and implement technical integrations with our other partners in the value chain (workflow orchestration, AI frameworks, etc.)

- Translate complex technical concepts into clear explanations for both developers and business audiences.

Why This Role Matters 

Every integration you build helps define how AI systems connect to live, trusted information .

You’ll operate on the frontier between customers and product - bringing the voice of the field into everything we build and say.

Your work will inform:

- The stories we tell in marketing.

- The use cases we automate in our GTM systems.

- The features we prioritize in our roadmap.

If you love blending engineering with impact - building things users actually depend on: this role is for you.

You’re a Great Fit If You 

- 2+ years in technical support engineering , software engineering , or solutions engineering , with direct application development experience.

- Strong API integration skills - able to design and debug REST/JSON payloads, manage auth flows, and optimize latency.

- Understand web infrastructure, distributed systems, or retrieval pipelines.

- Are comfortable debugging integrations and solving ambiguous technical challenges in customer environments.

- Communicate clearly and empathetically with both technical and business audiences.

- Are curious about AI infrastructure, retrieval, and the emerging agentic ecosystem.

- Thrive in a fast-paced, high-ownership startup environment.

Example Projects 

- Help a partner integrate Linkup’s /search endpoint into their multi-agent workflow.

- Build a proof-of-concept combining a customer’s private data with Linkup’s real-time web results.

- Collaborate with the backend team to improve SDK telemetry and enterprise deployment reliability.

- Work with the GTM team to turn successful integrations into published use cases and reference architectures.

- Identify recurring customer needs that can become productized templates or automation.

About Linkup 

Our Vision 

We believe in a future of AI agents and the agentic web . These digital entities can create more value for humanity than we ever could alone, but they depend on the internet to operate, collaborate, take action, and gather information.

AI agents need web search . To perform well, they require information that is current, reliable, and context‑specific—not the diffuse, steadily aging knowledge frozen at their last training cut‑off.

Modern web search is built for humans, not AIs . Instead of trusted facts, it serves links, ads, and click‑bait. People want visually engaging pages; AI systems need structured truth. An AI can absorb oceans of data, while human attention barely skims the surface. Humans think visually and intuitively; AI reasons in latent space.

Web 2.0 is sunsetting . The deck is being reshuffled, and the Bing‑Google search oligopoly is crumbling. Indexing ever more pages is no longer the goal; semantically organizing facts for AI systems is. In the coming agentic web, Google’s ad‑driven model has no natural home.

Search for AI must be rebuilt from the ground up . We are reconstructing the web as a rigorously structured knowledge layer, mapping every concept, entity, and claim into a coherent semantic graph. This foundation delivers verified facts and rich context to AI instantly, unlocking faster reasoning, higher accuracy, and radically more useful answers for everyone.

Humans search Google; AI searches Linkup. 

Our Mission 

Reality never stands still, and neither should intelligence. Linkup reconnects language models to a living stream of verified facts, ensuring AIs remain as current and insightful as the world they serve.

Our mission is to deliver the world’s freshest, most trusted knowledge to AIs.

Our Culture 

Our culture is built on the following values:

- Mission . We believe we play a critical role in building the agentic web. We are 100% committed to our mission of bringing the reality of the world to AI agents.

- Speed . We build fast, we build to last. We get things done, well.

- Ownership . We empower every team member to take ownership of their projects, ensuring they see them through to successful completion.

- Teamwork . Our strength lies in our unity. We rely on one another and embrace our diversity as a core asset.

- Humility . We maintain low egos, showing respect for others and continuously learning from their insights and experiences.

We expect all team member to take an active role in shaping our company culture.

Our Team 

We are small technical team, working shoulder to shoulder to build the web of agents.

A bit more about our 3 co-founders:

- Philippe Mizrahi - Led the development of Lyft’s Autonomous Vehicles marketplace. Previously launched Amundsen , an open source search engine.

- Denis Charrier - Founding Engineer at Niland, an audio search company (acquired by Spotify), then Staff Engineer at Spotify. 15y of software development experience.

- Boris Toledano - Led robotics at Carrefour, after 3y at McKinsey & Co working on public affairs and digital transformation.

title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer (Web + Infrastructure)
description:
Searoutes makes the emissions data that shippers use to run and reduce their
logistics. It is an operational problem before it is an environmental one, and
in our hands it is mostly an engineering one.

We are hiring a senior engineer who works across our web frontend and our
infrastructure — the same two codebases, in the same week. Someone who ships a
product screen on Monday, changes an identity-provider flow on Wednesday, and
considers those the same job.

We are looking for a broad profile rather than a specialist. The next year is
mostly platform work with a user-facing edge — user management, API gateway 
management, payments, SEO, and a great deal of compliance, GDPR and ISO 27001. 

If you are passionate about the environment, proactive and pragmatic in getting
things done, and love to work in a complex but fascinating industry where you
learn every day — then this is the place for you.

The work in front of us 

Some of the items on our tech roadmap for the coming year. Bets are picked a
cycle at a time and shared out, so you would take the ones that suit you and
grow into the rest.

- Product and marketing UI in React — multi-brand, WCAG AA, strong on
technical SEO, fast enough to hold a performance budget.
- User management and identity — Keycloak realms, organisation hierarchies,
partner brokering, and the entitlement model in the app.
- API gateway work in APISIX — routes, plugins and auth policy as code.
- Payments and billing. 
- ISO 27001 and GDPR — access control, change management, audit logging,
observability and alerting, consent and retention.
- The infrastructure underneath — Pulumi in TypeScript, Docker Swarm on
Hetzner, Cloudflare at the edge, Tailscale for all engineer and CI access.
- Third-party integrations — usually the seam between two systems that were
never designed to meet.

Nobody arrives fluent in all of that, and we are not expecting it. We want
someone strong across a good part of it, comfortable being new to the rest, and
used to working things out — with a team and with agents, rather than alone.

Also in daily use: Postgres and PostGIS, Valkey, ClickHouse; Vite, Tailwind and
Radix; Jest and Playwright; GitHub Actions; HAProxy. Most of what we write is
TypeScript, strict — though our core API is Java and Spring, and the identity
layer has Java in it too, so how far you go into that side is up to you.

How we work 

LLM-native, in the codebases you would work in. They are built around
agent-assisted development rather than merely tolerant of it — the conventions,
the tooling and the review gates all assume it. Agents do most of the
implementation and much of the review; humans design, verify and approve. What
we are really hiring for is judgement over output you did not write by hand :
knowing what to specify, what to check, and what to throw away. The bar did not
move when the tooling did.

Shape Up, and you own what you take. Roughly three weeks of building, then a
week of cooldown, with bets chosen at a betting table. We are small enough that
an area becomes yours quickly — you make the calls inside it and you answer for
how it turns out. We hand out problems, not the steps that solve them.

Remote first, with most of the team in Europe and everyone together in person at
least twice a year. Significant technical decisions get written down, and a
green build is never on its own enough to merge.

Requirements 

You'll thrive here if you have…

- Senior full-stack experience — you have owned features from the browser to
the machine they run on.
- A track record of taking something and running with it — a domain, a
migration, a subsystem you took on, decided and stayed accountable for.
- Taste. You can tell a good design from a merely plausible one, and you
will reject work that functions but is not right — your own, and an agent's.
- React beyond the client — server rendering, static generation, data
loading and hydration; you know what runs where and why it matters.
- TypeScript at strict — typed boundaries, and an instinct for when types
are carrying real weight.
- Infrastructure as code — Pulumi ideally; Terraform if you are ready to
pick up Pulumi.
- Containers and Linux in production — not writing a Dockerfile, but
debugging a service on a machine you have to SSH into.
- Postgres beyond queries — backup and restore, migrations, what a schema
change does under load.
- Wholehearted LLM-assisted development — you use coding agents daily, have
opinions about steering them, and review their output as critically as a
colleague's.
- Integration instincts — third-party APIs, webhooks, OAuth/OIDC, and
patience for other people's undocumented edge cases.
- A working day that overlaps ours : based within CET ±3.
- Fluent in English, our working language.

Nice to have 

- Identity and API gateways in depth — Keycloak, OIDC, SAML brokering, APISIX.
- Compliance from the inside — an ISO 27001 certification lived through, or GDPR
beyond a cookie banner.
- Payment systems, billing models, or PSP integrations.
- Observability and alerting — Prometheus, Grafana or equivalent.
- Experience in the maritime, logistics or freight industry.
- Familiarity with emissions accounting frameworks (GHG Protocol, GLEC, EU
ETS..).
Benefits 

As part of our team, you will:

- 🌱 Have a chance to re-shape the future of climate in the logistics.
- 👩‍💻 Be empowered to deliver your best work remotely, and get a stipend to set
you up.
- 🏄‍♂️ Have a flat hierarchy, where you will have direct access to the founders
and won't be tied up in politics.
- 🎓 Have a high degree of learning and ownership in a dynamic environment.
- 🏝 Take part in our team-building events.
