title: Staff Product Manager – Firefox Enterprise
description:
Why Mozilla 

Mozilla Corporation is a non-profit-backed technology company that has helped shape the internet for the better over the past 25 years. We’re the makers of Firefox , the privacy-focused web browser used by more than 225 million people around the world each month. As we look to the future, we’re working to shape the next 25 years of the internet—one that’s built for people, not just for profit. 

Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the 501(c) non-profit Mozilla Foundation , meaning we’re accountable not to shareholders, but to our mission. Alongside thousands of contributors and collaborators around the world, Mozillians design, build, and maintain open-source software that empowers people to use the internet on their own terms. 

About this team and role 

Firefox Enterprise is seeking a Staff Product Manager to own a major part of our 2027 product roadmap as we grow from our first release into a multi-product enterprise offering. This is a high-impact role for someone who has taken enterprise security products from zero to one. You will set direction, align engineering, design and go-to-market partners, and deliver. 

This role is ideal for someone who can work across teams with empathy, build trust with a wide range of partners, and move work forward in a practical, low-ego way. You will join a small product team, and work closely with engineering, security, legal, sales and customers, including our first enterprise pilots. You do not need to know browsers inside out, but you do need to bring structure to ambiguity, make clear product decisions, and follow through. 

What You’ll Do 

- Own the strategy, roadmap and delivery of a major Firefox Enterprise workstream in 2027, starting with our hosted offering alongside the existing on-premise solution 

- Define requirements, success metrics and release plans, and work with engineering, design, security and infrastructure teams to ship them 

- Work with pilot customers and prospects, including IT, security and compliance teams, to understand their deployment needs and turn them into prioritized product decisions

title: Site Reliability Engineer
description:
About Us: 

DeepJudge is Switzerland’s leading AI and ICT scale-up, transforming how law firms and legal departments access and leverage their knowledge. Founded by former Google search engineers with PhDs in AI from ETH Zurich, and backed by top-tier Silicon Valley investors, we are building the intelligence layer that powers the legal industry.

Every firm can license the same AI models, but no two firms share the same institutional knowledge. Decades of experience, work product, and precedent are often trapped across systems, underused and inaccessible. DeepJudge makes this expertise instantly available through world-class enterprise search and AI infrastructure, enabling firms to automate workflows, build knowledge-powered applications, and turn experience into a lasting advantage.

Our technology is trusted by many of the world’s leading law firms, including Freshfields, Gunderson Dettmer, Holland & Knight, Arent Fox, and Cozen O’Connor. Headquartered in Switzerland with a growing team across North America, we are expanding rapidly and shaping the future of how professional knowledge is discovered and applied.

At DeepJudge, we move fast, think rigorously, and care deeply about what we build. We combine cutting-edge research with close collaboration with our clients to deliver solutions that truly make an impact. If you want to be part of a team defining how AI transforms high-stakes knowledge work, this is the place to do it.

About the role: 

As a Site Reliability Engineer at DeepJudge, you own the reliability of the systems that leading law firms depend on every day. We run our AI search platform in dedicated production environments, each a large-scale search and retrieval system operating at very high data volumes, alongside our ingestion pipelines and data stores, on container-orchestrated infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds. Keeping those environments fast, available, and trustworthy is a genuine engineering challenge, and it's your mission.

This is a technical, infrastructure-focused role: you'll spend your time in systems, code, and telemetry. You'll harden the platform so that classes of failure can't recur, build observability and SLOs to let us see problems before they surface, plan capacity ahead of relentless data growth, and automate away the toil of safely operating many production environments. You'll work across our deployment and infrastructure-as-code and partner closely with product engineering to feed reliability learnings back into the platform. If you like operating serious distributed systems at scale and turning firefighting into engineered reliability, this role is for you.

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Owning the availability, latency and performance of our production environments: large-scale search and retrieval services, ingestion and data stores on container-orchestrated infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds

- Owning the cloud infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds, networking, identity and access, compute and storage, and managing cloud capacity, quotas and cost as the fleet grows

- Improving deployment and infrastructure through code: GitOps-based configuration and deployment and infrastructure-as-code across our public and private clouds, with safe, previewed, recoverable production changes

- Defining and instrumenting SLOs and error budgets and building the dashboards, metrics and alerting that make production observable and actionable

- Reducing operational toil through automation and internal tooling written in Python and / or Go

- Provisioning and standardizing new production environments to a defined reliability bar

You're a great fit if you: 

- Have 3+ years in SRE, production / platform engineering, or infrastructure-heavy software engineering, operating real production systems under reliability expectations

- Are strong at container-orchestration operations in production and comfortable on at least one major public cloud

- Have solid cloud infrastructure experience on a major public cloud and a working grasp of cloud capacity, quotas, and cost

- Practice observability hands-on with metrics, logs and traces, and use it to root-cause live incidents

- Work fluently with infrastructure-as-code and GitOps

- Can code in Python and / or Go for automation, tooling, and reading and patching service code.

- Bring sound production judgment and document your work clearly for other engineers

- Bonus: experience operating a large-scale search or distributed data system, database operations, dedicated / enterprise-deployed software, or AI / enterprise-search infrastructure in regulated domains

What you can look forward to: 

- Owning the reliability of systems that the world's leading law firms rely on: real scale, real impact

- Deep, hands-on work with modern infrastructure: distributed search at very large scale, container orchestration across multiple clouds, and a mature infrastructure-as-code and GitOps stack

- A rigorous, high-urgency engineering culture founded by ex-Google search engineers and ETH Zurich AI PhDs

- The chance to build the reliability discipline, SLOs, incident practice, automation, from a strong foundation, not inherit a rigid one

- A collaborative team in Zurich shaping how AI transforms professional knowledge work

title: Scientific Account Executive
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the role

This is a hybrid sales and customer success role for someone with real scientific depth. You'll be the primary point of contact for customers — from first conversation through ongoing engagement. That means understanding what a protein design team is actually trying to achieve, helping them pick the right assays, making sure their experiments are set up correctly, and translating results back into language that's useful for their programs.

The day-to-day:

- Running technical sales calls where you discuss binding kinetics, expression systems, and assay design, not just pricing

- Onboarding new customers and helping them design their first experiments on the platform

- Monitoring ongoing accounts, flagging issues early, and proactively suggesting next steps based on their results

- Working with the biology team to troubleshoot when a customer's experiment doesn't go as expected

- Identifying expansion opportunities within existing accounts — new targets, new assay types, larger campaigns

You won't be handed a script. You'll need to understand the science well enough to earn trust from PhD-level protein engineers and CSOs, while also being commercially sharp enough to close deals and grow accounts.

Responsibilities 

- Own the full customer lifecycle: prospecting, technical sales conversations, deal closing, onboarding, and ongoing account management.

- Serve as the technical point of contact for customers. Understand their protein engineering goals and recommend the right experiments (binding, expression, thermostability, enzyme activity).

- Understand and explain our assay capabilities in depth: BLI, SPR, cell-free expression, and emerging assay types. Know when each is appropriate and what the data means.

- Work closely with the biology team to ensure experiments are designed correctly and results are communicated clearly.

- Build and maintain a pipeline of commercial opportunities across customer segments: AI-driven protein design companies, biotech startups, pharma R&D teams, and academic labs.

- Develop proposals and quotes tailored to customer needs, from small pilot experiments to large-scale data generation campaigns.

- Represent Adaptyv at conferences and industry events. Be able to have deep technical conversations at the booth, not just hand out brochures.

- Feed customer insights back to the product and biology teams: what assays are people asking for, what's missing, where are we losing deals.

What we're looking for 

- Scientific background in protein engineering, biochemistry, biophysics, or a related field. You should be comfortable discussing binding kinetics (KD, kon, koff), expression systems, and assay design without needing to look things up.

- Experience in a customer-facing technical role: field application scientist, technical sales, scientific account management, or similar. CRO or biotech vendor experience is a strong plus.

- Commercially driven. You care about revenue, pipeline, and closing deals, not just having interesting scientific conversations.

- Strong communicator who can adapt to the audience: detailed and technical with a scientist, concise and business-focused with a VP.

- Self-starter who can manage their own pipeline and priorities without heavy oversight.

- Genuine interest in AI-driven protein design and the companies working in this space. You follow what's happening in the field.

Application deadline 

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

- Build anomaly detection and QC models that catch bad data the eye would miss: assay drift, instrument variability, plate effects, false passes and false fails — and distinguish real signal from noise statistically.

- Work with the software and ML teams to specify, review, and improve the automated data pipelines that process instrument outputs, feeding back precise requirements for what to flag, auto-reject, or route to human review.

- Connect experimental results back to the protein side — sequence, structure, and design — so wet-lab data and computational models reinforce each other.

- Turn foundry output into structured, documented, benchmark-grade datasets that are a genuine asset for our customers and for training and evaluating protein-design models.

- Apply real statistical rigor to multi-condition data at scale — thousands of samples across hundreds of simultaneous experiments — and make the results interpretable and comparable across runs.

- AI-native builder. It's 2026 — you build with coding agents like Claude Code as a default, and you have sharp judgment about what they produce.

That person is you.

The second half of the job is talking to the customer about it. When a design team gets a plate back and three of their best predictions look like non-binders, they want to talk to someone who can explain why: reference subtraction, avidity, an off-rate at the edge of what the instrument resolves, or simply a bad protein. What You'll Do

- Review the binding data coming out of the lab. Every SPR and BLI run passes through our processing pipeline and then to human review, and you're the expert eye on the output. You decide what gets delivered, what gets flagged, and what gets re-run.

- Judge the curves, not just the numbers. A clean-looking Kd on a bad fit is worse than no number at all. You know the difference between a real off-rate and a drifting baseline, and you can say why.

- Review data from our other assays too: thermostability, expression, developability, enzyme activity. Binding is the core of the role but it isn't all of it.

- Talk to customers about their results. Deliverable walkthroughs, follow-up questions, and the awkward conversation when the data doesn't say what they hoped. You explain what we measured, how confident we are, and what to do next.

- Turn review into experimental design. When something needs a re-run, you decide what changes: orientation, regeneration, concentration series, or a switch from BLI to SPR for the sensitivity.

- Analyze at the batch level, not just the sample level. With hundreds of results per experiment, you should be writing a script to find the pattern rather than clicking through a queue. Systematic drift, a bad reference channel, or a target lot behaving differently than the last one shows up in aggregate long before it shows up in any single curve.

- Feed what you learn back into the pipeline. When you catch a case where automation passed something it shouldn't have, or failed something it shouldn't have, that becomes a concrete requirement for the software team.

It is also most of what a protein costs to make, which makes procurement one of the biggest levers on gross margin in the business.

So far scientists have bought what they need, decisions get made in hours, and nothing blocks an experiment. That was the right trade while we were proving the thing works. But we are multiplying lab throughput several times over, and at that volume procurement becomes a discipline: real terms with the suppliers we already buy from heavily, qualified second sources where we currently have one, inventory that is planned rather than remembered. Nobody has taken that on yet.

You would be our first dedicated supply chain hire, and it is hands-on — you do the sourcing and the negotiating yourself. One thing makes it harder than a typical procurement job: our assay portfolio keeps expanding, and every new assay brings new reagents. You are not optimizing a static supply chain, you are building one that flexes with the science. How far the role goes from there is up to you.

What You'll Do

- Own procurement end to end. Every input to the lab, from gene synthesis down to gloves. Requests, POs, receiving, vendor onboarding, the lot.

- De-risk the supply chain. Too much of what we depend on has exactly one supplier. Find second sources, qualify them properly with the science team, and keep them warm, so that switching is a decision we make rather than an emergency we react to.

- Negotiate. Build the supplier relationships across our DNA, reagent, biosensor and catalog-protein vendors, put volume commitments and pricing agreements in place, and go get the margin back.

- Drive down the cost of a protein. Go category by category and take cost out of each. A few francs per protein, multiplied across the volumes we are heading toward, is a seven-figure line.

- Stay ahead of the science. When R&D says they are adding a new assay next quarter, you should already be sourcing the reagents for it.

- Set inventory policy, and make the numbers true. Reorder points and safety stock, so we never stall a customer experiment on a stockout and never have six figures of reagents quietly expiring in a freezer. You decide what should be on the shelves and how much of it.

- Plan supply for the lab expansion. Model what several-fold throughput actually needs — volumes, lead times, storage, cash tied up in stock — and have it in place before the capacity comes online, not after.

- Own landed cost. Shipping, customs, import duties, VAT recoverability, cold chain. We import a lot of biology into Switzerland and both the cost and the failure modes matter.

- Own COGS with Finance. Procurement and finance are the two halves of gross margin, and you are the procurement half.

- Automate the whole thing. Ordering, tracking, and reconciliation should mostly run themselves.

What We're Looking For

- You have worked in supply chain or procurement in a physical, technical business. Biotech, a CRO, or another life science company is ideal, and you understand reagent categories — enzymes, antibodies, media, resins, plasticware — and how they are actually sourced. Hardware manufacturing or another high-mix production setting translates well. Buying software licences does not. You do not need to have run a supply chain organization before; you do need to be ready to own one.

- You think in margins. Saving a few francs per protein across tens of thousands of proteins a month is a number that should make you sit up.

- You are technical enough to talk to scientists. You do not need a degree in biology, but you will be qualifying an alternative supplier for a reagent that a protein biochemist depends on, and you need to be able to have that conversation properly rather than forwarding it.

- You can negotiate. Comfortable sitting across from vendors who have been selling into labs for thirty years, and comfortable walking away.

- You automate. We run on Claude Code across the company and our lab system has an API. Some of our largest suppliers still require a human to upload a spreadsheet to a portal, and we consider that a bug rather than a fact of life. The best version of this person is writing scripts against our systems and our vendors' systems, not clicking through them. If your instinct is that procurement is a portal-and-email job, we will frustrate each other.

- Obsessive about the details that bite. Lead times, expiry dates, lot numbers, minimum order quantities. Nothing falls through.

- You want to grow fast. We are going from roughly 25 people to roughly 50 in the next year, and the lab spend grows faster than the headcount does.

- Swiss or EU import/export experience is a strong plus.

Scope

We are a small company and nobody here has clean edges around their job. You will end up in the lab, in a spreadsheet with Finance, on the phone with a courier, and every so often doing something that is nobody's job simply because it needs doing. That is the deal, and if it sounds unappealing then we are probably not the right place.

What we do want to be clear about is where the centre of gravity is. This role is about what we buy, who we buy it from, what we pay, and how reliably it turns up. Sourcing, negotiation, supplier relationships, inventory, resilience, cost. One thing it is not: an order-taking job. You are not a mailbox between scientists and vendors. You decide what we source and from whom, and we expect you to argue with us about it.

Why This Role Is Interesting

Most supply chain jobs are about keeping a stable system stable. This one is about building the supply chain for a lab that is about to grow several-fold, at a company where the cost and reliability of an experiment more or less is the product. Every franc you take out of the cost of a protein, and every week you take out of a lead time, shows up directly in what we can offer customers and in whether AI-designed biology is cheap enough to be worth doing at scale. There are not many procurement jobs where the leverage is that direct, or that visible to the people running the company.

title: Synthesis Instrumentation Engineer
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

We're looking for a hands-on scientist-engineer to help build our next-generation DNA synthesis platform, enabling high-throughput, cost-effective production of large and diverse DNA libraries. You'll work at the intersection of chemistry, materials science, bioengineering, and hardware development, designing and building prototypes, running experiments, and optimizing processes to turn new synthesis technologies into reliable, scalable production systems.

DNA synthesis is a fundamental part of our protein engineering platform. We're developing new approaches to dramatically increase synthesis throughput while reducing cost and turnaround time.

You'll work closely with our scientific and engineering teams to develop and prototype new DNA synthesis technologies. Your focus will be on translating scientific concepts into working hardware and experimental systems, designing and building prototypes, testing different approaches, and continuously improving their performance.

This is a highly hands-on, interdisciplinary role combining experimental science with practical engineering. You'll take ownership of prototype development, experimental validation, and process optimization, helping move promising technologies from early concepts to reliable, scalable systems.

We're looking for someone who enjoys building things, solving technical problems, and working across disciplines. You don't need to be an expert in DNA synthesis, but you should have strong scientific fundamentals, an engineering mindset, and experience turning ideas into working prototypes.

What You'll Do

- Design, build, and test prototypes for next-generation DNA synthesis technologies.

- Translate scientific and technical requirements into practical engineering designs and experimental setups.

- Scope and evaluate different technical approaches, components, materials, and equipment for prototype development.

- Develop and optimize the chemistry, materials, and processes underlying the synthesis platform.

- Design and execute experiments to characterize performance, identify limitations, and improve reliability.

- Work closely with mechanical, electronics, software, and automation engineers to develop integrated experimental systems.

- Troubleshoot complex technical problems across chemistry, hardware, and process engineering.

- Develop analytical methods and quality control strategies to measure performance and guide optimization.

- Help scale successful prototypes into robust, reproducible systems suitable for routine production.

- Work with external suppliers and engineering partners to source components, evaluate technologies, and accelerate development.

What We're Looking For

- A strong background in chemical engineering, chemistry, materials science, bioengineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field.

- Hands-on experience designing, building, and testing experimental setups, prototypes, or laboratory equipment.

- Strong understanding of chemistry, materials, or process engineering, with the ability to apply these fundamentals to practical engineering challenges.

- Experience developing and optimizing experimental processes, including systematic troubleshooting and performance characterization.

- Comfortable working across hardware and experimental science, translating scientific requirements into practical engineering solutions.

- Experience selecting components, evaluating technical trade-offs, and iterating on prototype designs.

- Strong experimental skills, including designing experiments, analyzing data, and making decisions based on results.

- Independent, resourceful, and comfortable working on open-ended technical problems.

- A practical, hands-on approach to engineering, with a focus on building, testing, and improving systems rather than purely theoretical development.

- Experience with DNA or oligonucleotide synthesis, including chemical or enzymatic approaches, is a plus.

- Experience with solid-phase synthesis, surface chemistry, or chemical process development is a plus.

- Familiarity with microfluidics, high-throughput dispensing, or array-based technologies is a plus.

- Experience with laboratory automation, instrumentation, or custom hardware development is a plus.

- Experience with CAD, electronics, fluidics, or mechanical prototyping is a plus.

- Experience scaling experimental technologies from proof of concept to production is a plus.

- Programming and data analysis experience, particularly in Python, is a plus.

📍 Amsterdam - Hybride (minimaal 50% op kantoor)

💰 € 4100 - €5100 per maand (op basis van een 40-urige werkweek) 

🌍 Futurewhiz is een B Corp 

Hoe maak je leren zo leuk dat kinderen verder willen ontdekken? Bij Squla combineer je technologie, spel en kinderpsychologie om digitale leerervaringen te ontwerpen die de wereld van kinderen vergroot. Hun enthousiasme, onverwachte vragen en eerlijke reacties maken kinderen een geweldige doelgroep om voor te werken. 

We werken aan een totale vernieuwing van Squla. Als Product Designer onderzoek je wat kinderen, ouders en leerkrachten nodig hebben, verken en test je nieuwe concepten en werk je die samen met het team uit. Je grootste kracht ligt in onderzoek en het verkennen en testen van ideeën, en met jouw ontwerpvaardigheden breng je de ideeën tot leven. 

🏰 Onze missie 

Bij Futurewhiz bouwen we digitale leerproducten die kinderen en jongeren helpen groeien. Met merken als Squla en StudyGo ondersteunen we honderdduizenden leerlingen bij hun ontwikkeling. Als B Corp combineren we commerciële groei met maatschappelijke impact. 

Squla helpt basisschoolkinderen leren door middel van games, quizzen en interactieve oefeningen die aansluiten op het Nederlandse onderwijs. Met onze productvernieuwing bouwen we aan de volgende fase van Squla. Jij helpt ontdekken welke leerervaringen daarin het verschil kunnen maken. 

🎮 Wat ga je doen? 

Bij Squla werk je aan vragen als: Hoe help je een kind na een fout weer op weg? Wat maakt een oefening uitdagend zonder frustrerend te worden? Hoe zorg ik dat de vorm bijdraagt aan het leereffect? 

Als product designer bij Squla werk je aan het volledige ontwerpproces: van gebruikersonderzoek en conceptvalidatie tot UX- en UI-design en implementatie. Je maakt ideeën tastbaar, werkt interacties en visuele details uit en bouwt samen met het team aan het vernieuwde Squla. 

🌟 Jouw rol en impact 

Jij bent een Product designer die energie krijgt van: 

- Doelgroep begrijpen: Je spreekt kinderen, ouders en leerkrachten, bezoekt scholen en combineert observaties met gedrags- en gebruiksdata. 

- Nieuwe concepten verkennen en testen: Je vertaalt inzichten naar kansen en ideeën. Je maakt aannames expliciet en kiest passende experimenten en prototypes om te onderzoeken of een concept begrijpelijk, aantrekkelijk en waardevol is. 

- Ontwerpen en doorontwikkelen: Je werkt kansrijke ideeën uit tot journeys, flows, interacties en visuele ontwerpen, met aandacht voor gebruiksgemak, toegankelijkheid en consistentie. 

- Bijdragen aan implementatie: Je werkt ontwerpen samen met Engineering uit tot werkende productervaringen. Waar passend kun je zelf vibecoden om wijzigingen in de productcode te maken, met review door Engineering. 

- Leren van resultaten: Je gebruikt feedback, tests en gebruiksdata om te beoordelen of je ontwerp werkt en wat beter kan. 

Je werkt samen met collega’s uit Product, Engineering, Educatie, Data, Marketing en Design. Je wordt ook onderdeel van de design guild binnen Futurewhiz: een plek om design werk te bespreken, kennis te delen en elkaar te helpen groeien. 

🔥 Wie ben jij? 

Je bent een Product Designer die graag uitzoekt waarom mensen iets nodig hebben en hoe een ontwerp daarop kan aansluiten. Je voelt je prettig wanneer een vraagstuk nog open is en weet onderzoek om te zetten in concrete vervolgstappen. 

Daarnaast: 

- Je hebt 3+ jaar ervaring als Product Designer, UX Designer of UX/UI Designer en hebt digitale producten ontworpen en opgeleverd in een multidisciplinair team. 

- Je kunt zelfstandig onderzoek doen: onderzoeksvragen formuleren, passende onderzoeksmethoden kiezen, uitvoering en bevindingen vertalen naar ontwerpkeuzes. 

- Je begrijpt het verschil tussen wat gebruikers zeggen, wat ze doen en wat je daaruit kunt concluderen. 

- Je verkent meerdere ideeën voordat je een richting kiest en gebruikt prototypes om snel te leren. 

- Je hebt goede vaardigheden in UI design, visueel ontwerp en prototyping, bij voorkeur met Figma. 

- Je kunt gebruikersbehoeften afwegen tegen leerdoelen, productdoelen en technische mogelijkheden. 

- Je legt je keuzes helder uit, staat open voor feedback en neemt verantwoordelijkheid voor de kwaliteit van je werk. 

- Je kunt vibecoden en gebruikt AI-designtools om concepten, werkende prototypes en productaanpassingen te maken. Je beoordeelt de uitkomsten kritisch en zorgt samen met Engineering voor kwaliteit en haalbaarheid. 

- Je beheerst Nederlands en Engels goed, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk. Je kunt onderzoek uitvoeren met Nederlandstalige kinderen, ouders en leerkrachten en inzichten helder delen met je Engelstalige collega’s. 

In je portfolio zien we graag hoe je van onderzoek naar inzicht, concept en validatie bent gekomen, welke keuzes je hebt gemaakt en wat je daarvan hebt geleerd. 

Ervaring met onderzoek onder kinderen, EdTech, digitale consumentenproducten of spelenderwijs leren is een pré. 

💰 Wat krijg je van ons? 

- Salaris, € 4100 - €5100 per maand (op basis van een 40-urige werkweek) 

- 24 vrije vakantiedagen + 1 ‘spijbeldag’ (vrije dag) + 3 toegewezen vakantiedagen 

- Collectief pensioen en collectieve zorgverzekering 

- Een jaarlijks leerbudget van €600 voor jouw professionele ontwikkeling 

- Onbeperkt toegang tot externe coaches via Inuka Coaching 

- Onbeperkt toegang tot Goodhabitz voor professionele- en persoonlijke groei 

Daarnaast: 

- Levenslange toegang tot StudyGo en Squla-accounts 

- Kantoor naast station Amsterdam Bijlmer Arena (met een Swapfiets of OV-businesscard als je >7km van het kantoor woont) 

- Een MacBook om mee te werken 

- Een optie tot Payroll Giving om bij te dragen aan een goed doel 

- Gezonde lunches op kantoor, onbeperkt goede koffie, vers fruit en snacks 

- Een Culture Crew die leuke activiteiten organiseert zoals uitjes, pubquizzen en skireizen. 

😻 Wie zijn wij? 

Wij zijn een gepassioneerd en divers team, samengebracht door een gedeelde missie: kinderen helpen om te groeien in hun leerproces en hen te versterken met gepersonaliseerd onderwijs. 

Onze cultuur is open en authentiek – we geloven dat je het beste werk levert als je jezelf kunt zijn. Of je nu van boekenclubs, maandelijkse borrels, filmavonden, bakwedstrijden, Mario Kart-competities of skireizen houdt, bij Futurewhiz vind je een gemeenschap die als thuis voelt. 

Onze platforms zijn voor iedereen, en dat geldt ook voor onze werkplek. 

De kracht zit in onze verschillende achtergronden, ideeën, ervaringen en perspectieven. Deze diversiteit helpt ons om alle kinderen te ondersteunen in hun leerproces, ongeacht wie zij – of wij – zijn. Bij Futurewhiz omarmen we elkaars verschillen en creëren we een authentieke werkomgeving waarin iedereen zichzelf kan zijn. Zo maken we het ook makkelijker voor anderen om dat te doen. We zijn toegewijd aan een diverse en inclusieve cultuur, die begint op ons kantoor en zich uitstrekt over al onze platforms – en iedereen is welkom op deze reis. 

Word jij onze nieuwe Product Designer? 

We nodigen je graag uit om te solliciteren, ook als je niet aan alle vereisten voldoet, maar wel enthousiast bent. 

Tip: wees vooral jezelf. We omarmen de diversiteit van al onze collega’s en zijn oprecht benieuwd naar jouw unieke perspectief

Heb je het gevoel dat je als calculator meer kunt dan je nu laat zien? En zoek je een omgeving waar je wordt uitgedaagd met complexere projecten, meer verantwoordelijkheid en ruimte om echt mee te denken?

Bij HulstFlier werk je aan projecten waar jouw technisch inzicht het verschil maakt. Geen standaard invuloefening, maar projecten waarin je installaties moet doorgronden, keuzes maakt en bepaalt wat een slimme en haalbare aanpak is. Je werkt aan verschillende soorten projecten, zoals utiliteitsprojecten, grote appartement complexen, parkeergarages, kantoren, industriële omgevingen en het verduurzamen van bestaande gebouwen. Projecten waarin je echt wordt uitgedaagd en waarin jouw ervaring en inzicht bepalend zijn voor het resultaat.

Je duikt in tekeningen, bestekken en technische omschrijvingen en vertaalt dit naar een kostprijs die klopt. Daarbij kijk je niet alleen naar hoeveelheden, maar vooral naar hoe het daadwerkelijk gemaakt wordt. Je begrijpt hoe installaties worden opgebouwd en waar het in de uitvoering mis kan gaan.

Als senior calculator neem je hierin vanzelfsprekend de lead. Je overziet het geheel, stelt prioriteiten en maakt keuzes die impact hebben op het project. Je bent een inhoudelijke sparringpartner voor projectleiders, engineers en opdrachtgevers. Je werkt met onder andere warmtepompen, duurzame systemen, ventilatie en andere HVAC-installaties, maar ook met loodgieterswerk en sanitairtechniek. Daarnaast denk je mee over energieconcepten en nieuwe oplossingen. Je hebt daarin de ruimte om creatief te zijn en samen met opdrachtgevers te bepalen wat technisch en praktisch haalbaar is, binnen budget.

Je bepaalt hoeveel materiaal, uren en middelen nodig zijn en maakt daarin bewuste keuzes. Welke oplossing is technisch het beste? Wat is praktisch uitvoerbaar? Waar zitten risico’s en waar juist kansen? Je vraagt offertes op bij leveranciers en onderaannemers en beoordeelt deze inhoudelijk. Je ziet snel waar iets niet klopt of niet compleet is en stelt de juiste vragen.

Je werkt nauw samen met projectleiders, engineers en de E afdeling. Het is een samenspel tussen disciplines, waarin jij een belangrijke rol speelt in het maken van de juiste keuzes. Wat jij berekent, moet buiten gewoon werken. Daarnaast kijk je mee in de nacalculatie en gebruik je die inzichten om continu te verbeteren. Je werkt aan meerdere projecten tegelijk en houdt overzicht, ook als het complex wordt.

Juist in die complexiteit zit voor jou de uitdaging. En wil je daarin verder groeien, bijvoorbeeld richting nog grotere projecten of meer verantwoordelijkheid binnen het team, dan krijg je daar ook de ruimte voor.

“Als calculator ben je als eerste betrokken bij een project. Je maakt plannen werkelijkheid en stuurt bij op haalbaarheid, zowel technisch als qua budget. Juist dat maakt het werk uitdagend.” 

Maarten Westerveld, Calculator HulstFlier 

Werken bij HulstFlier 

HulstFlier is een installatiebedrijf waar vakmanschap en samenwerken centraal staan. We werken met korte lijnen, houden van duidelijkheid en zorgen dat afspraken worden nagekomen.

Wat mensen hier waarderen, is dat het gewoon klopt. De basis is goed geregeld, je kunt op elkaar rekenen en collega’s helpen elkaar vooruit. Dat betekent voor jou dat je in een omgeving komt waar je snel je plek vindt en de ruimte krijgt om je werk goed te doen en jezelf te blijven ontwikkelen. 

Je standplaats is Zwolle, maar je werkt ook samen met collega’s in Elburg. Daarnaast is deels thuiswerken mogelijk, mits je daar een goede werkplek hebt.

Je komt terecht in een team van calculators (E en WTB), waarin je samenwerkt maar ook ruimte krijgt om je eigen rol te pakken. Heb je ambities om op termijn meer verantwoordelijkheid te nemen of een leidende rol te pakken binnen het team, dan is daar ruimte voor. We zijn serieus over ons werk, maar er is ook ruimte voor een grapje. Iedereen draagt bij en samen zorgen we voor het resultaat.

Wat je van ons kunt verwachten 

- Een goed salaris dat past bij jouw ervaring. De salarisrange ligt tussen €4.500.- en €6.000,- bruto per maand.

- 25 vakantiedagen en 13 ADV dagen

- 8% vakantiegeld

- Ruimte voor scholing, opleiding en ontwikkeling, zodat je kunt blijven groeien in je rol

En laten we eerlijk zijn: werken is belangrijk, maar hoe je samen afsluit zegt alles over de sfeer. Op vrijdag schuif je aan voor een gezamenlijke lunch en één keer per maand sluiten we af met een borrel op kantoor.

Dus: wil jij presteren en vind je teamgevoel belangrijk? Dan pas je perfect bij ons!

Wat we belangrijk vinden 

We zoeken een ervaren calculator die zijn vak verstaat en toe is aan een volgende stap.

Daarbij vinden we het belangrijk dat je: 

- Technische kennis hebt op mbo+ of hbo-niveau, richting installatietechniek

- Installaties echt begrijpt en verder kijkt dan alleen de cijfers

Daarnaast ben je iemand die:

Je hoeft niet perfect te zijn, maar je hebt wel de drive om jezelf te blijven ontwikkelen.

title: Engineering Manager
description:
About Tekmetric 

Tekmetric is the all-in-one, cloud-based software helping auto repair shops run smarter, grow faster, and serve customers better. 

Built by a shop owner and shaped by the needs of the industry, Tekmetric brings together innovation, real-world experience, and a thriving community to help shops thrive - not just survive. From running a shop, to securing payments to engaging customers, our platform simplifies operations so shop owners can focus on what really matters: delivering exceptional service, earning trust, and growing sustainably.

Officially founded in Houston in 2017, Tekmetric has grown from a single shop’s vision to the industry’s leading solution - all by staying true to our values of transparency, integrity, innovation, and a service-first mindset. 

But we’re not just building shop management software. We’re building a movement. We’re empowering repair shops to rise above the daily grind, create meaningful connections with their customers, and lead the industry forward - one interaction at a time.

Come build with us. Join the journey. Shape the future of auto repair.

Working the Tekmetric Way 

At Tekmetric, we’re building a culture where winning matters - not for ego, but because when our customers win, we win together. 

We move fast, stay curious, and take full ownership of our results — no excuses, no finger-pointing. If you thrive in ambiguity, take initiative, and view honest feedback as fuel for growth, you’ll feel right at home here.

We’re direct but respectful, ambitious yet grounded, and collaborative at every level. Everyone leads through impact and is encouraged to speak up, share ideas, and challenge assumptions (even your manager’s). This is a place for builders, not bystanders.

Success here takes focus, follow-through, and a willingness to roll up your sleeves — but if you’re driven by meaningful work and real results, it’s deeply rewarding. You’ll join a team that cares about the work, supports one another, and takes smart risks to achieve bold goals. Be yourself, stay mission-focused, and you’ll thrive. If that energizes you, we can’t wait to meet you.

Where We Work : At Tekmetric, great work happens anywhere, but great teams are built through intentional connection. We offer hybrid and remote work models based on your proximity to our office hubs. Because we value in-person collaboration, travel is an expected part of every role. We come together several times a year for team and company-wide offsites to align on goals and strengthen relationships. Attendance at these events is expected and fully supported.

What You’ll Do 

As an Engineering Manager, you'll be responsible for leading a team of engineers in the design, development, and implementation of our products. You'll play a key role in guiding the technical direction of our projects, ensuring the highest quality of engineering work, and supporting the professional growth of your team members.

- Lead and mentor a team of engineers, providing technical guidance and career development support

- Foster a collaborative and inclusive team environment

- Own your team’s delivery, quality and timely execution

- Guide key technical decisions around new product initiatives

- Work closely with other departments, including product, design, and QA, to align engineering activities with company objectives

- Continuously evaluate and improve engineering processes and practices to enhance team efficiency and product quality

- Assist in recruiting, onboarding, and training new engineering team members

What You’ll Bring 

- 7+ years in software development with at least 2 years of engineering leadership experience

- You have built and developed an impactful team of passionate engineers

- You are able to tackle sophisticated engineering problems that deliver results which help the team to achieve its objectives

- You’re passionate about being in a product-focused environment where everyone cares deeply about customer impact

Why You'll Love Working With Us 

Health & Wellness That Have You Covered: 

- Enjoy the flexibility of remote work

- Competitive base salaries that reflect your value.

- Flexible PTO — No set number of days, just the trust to take the time you need. We genuinely encourage our team to disconnect and recharge.

- Support for every stage of life—with paid maternity, parental bonding, and medical leave for you or your loved ones.

- Comprehensive health benefits, including Medical, Dental, Vision, and Prescription coverage. For employee only, we offer plans that cover 100% of premiums and we cover 50% of costs for families.

- Prioritizing your mental health: get free, confidential counseling through our partnership with BetterHelp.

Investing in Your Future (and Present): 

- 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan with 100% employer match on contributions up to 6% - so your future self will thank you.

- Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) and Health Savings Accounts (HSA) to make your money go further.

- Life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) Insurance for added peace of mind.

- Wellness on your terms: get up to $60/month toward fitness, mental health, or almost anything that helps you feel your best.

- After one year of employment, enjoy a $300 home office setup bonus to help make your space work for you. 

- Keep growing with support for continuing education - we’re invested in your development.

Most importantly, we have a stellar team, a whole lot of fun, and work that actually matters to the shops and families we serve!

Tekmetric is an equal opportunity employer. We hire hard-working individuals, regardless of gender, race or color, ethnicity or national origin, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. We know that when our employees feel appreciated and included, they can be more creative, innovative and successful. 

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. 

Tekmetric will never ask for your personal financial or banking information or require any financial commitment as part of our candidate search or application process. No job offers will be made without a formal interview process. All legitimate Tekmetric job postings are listed at tekmetric.com/careers . title: Senior Software Engineer, Add-Ons
description:
Why Mozilla ? 

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.
The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

About this team and role: 

addons.mozilla.org (AMO) is the foundation of the Firefox add-ons ecosystem. It’s a showcase for developers to publish and grow their extensions, and a place of discovery for millions of users who customize Firefox to make it their own. Behind the scenes are the DevHub which enables developers to manage their extensions. To manage the ecosystem there are a series of Reviewer tools and automated moderation systems. 

As a Senior Software Engineer, you’ll bring a passion for crafting resilient systems that accelerate our review and moderation teams to provide a first-class experience for Add-on developers. You’ll work closely with engineers, reviewers, developer support, and Add-ons leadership to turn ideas into polished features, modernize the platform and its architecture, and see your work reach millions of people around the world.

What you’ll do: 

- Deliver major features and architectural improvements across the Add-ons stack, including automated moderation pipelines, Reviewer tools, and DevHub.

- Help establish and maintain engineering standards across areas such as code review, definition of done, production readiness, runbooks, incident response, on-call practices, coding conventions, and infrastructure as code.

- Create robust observability systems and data-backed insights.

- Provide peer feedback, share knowledge and help others grow.

- Build and improve the systems that enable Add-ons engineering to safely develop, deploy, observe, and operate production services.

- Improve our CI/CD pipelines using declarative, pipeline-as-code approaches that make changes reproducible, testable, and easy to review.

- Deliver work iteratively using a visible backlog, short feedback cycles, retrospectives, and demonstrations to stakeholders.

- Write clear technical documentation, including design notes, Architecture Decision Records, runbooks, and incident write-ups.

- Work effectively in unfamiliar codebases, tracing requests and asynchronous jobs end-to-end to understand failures and identify opportunities for improvement.

- Collaborate with designers, product managers, QA, and community contributors to deliver end-to-end improvements.

- Contribute in the open through pull requests, code reviews, and discussions.

- Work on:

- Feature development: submission flows, trust and safety signals, DevHub and Reviewer tools modernization.

- AMO application systems: Work within our Python/Django, MySQL, React/TypeScript, and asynchronous processing systems.

- Internal developer platforms : Create tools and paved paths that make it easier for teams to ship and operate software safely and consistently.

- Team Process: Contribute to team ceremonies, execute process improvement, and provide feedback on team effectiveness. 

- Engineering standards : Help make production readiness, testing, recoverability, documentation, and safe deployment part of the normal development lifecycle. 

- Platform reliability: Deployments, monitoring, and incident response.

What you’ll bring: 

- Strong hands-on experience building and maintaining production applications with Python/Django.

- Experience operating and improving production software systems where reliability and safe delivery matter.

- Strong experience with CI/CD systems and treating pipelines and infrastructure declaratively as code.

- Experience designing or improving automated testing and deployment workflows, including integration testing and staged or progressive delivery.

- Strong understanding of observability as an engineering discipline, including metrics, logging, tracing, service-level objectives, and actionable alerting.

- Experience building or maintaining internal tools or platforms used by other engineering teams, with an understanding that internal systems have users, reliability expectations, roadmaps, and lifecycle considerations.

- Experience defining or improving engineering practices such as code review standards, operational readiness, runbooks, incident response, on-call expectations, or definitions of done.

- Ability to read and understand unfamiliar codebases and trace application behavior across frontend, backend, asynchronous jobs, data stores, and infrastructure.

- Experience debugging complex production issues and turning what you learn into lasting system improvements.

- Strong technical writing skills, with experience creating useful documentation such as design documents, ADRs, runbooks, and incident reports.

- Experience working iteratively with a visible backlog, regular stakeholder feedback, and retrospectives that result in concrete improvements.

- Strong collaboration and communication skills in a distributed team environment.

- A willingness to share knowledge and mentor peers in operational and reliability practices.

- Commitment to our values:

- Welcoming differences

- Being relationship-minded

- Practicing responsible participation

- Having grit

Bonus points for: 

- Experience with Google Cloud and operating Kubernetes.

- Experience with infrastructure-as-code tooling and policy-as-code.

- Experience establishing SLOs and error-budget-based reliability practices.

- Experience with chaos engineering, disaster recovery testing, or production readiness reviews.

- Experience with trust and safety, automated moderation, abuse prevention, or other adversarial systems.

- Contributions to open source projects

What you’ll get: 

- Generous performance-based bonus plans to all eligible employees - we share in our success as one team

- Rich medical, dental, and vision coverage

- Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute)

- Quarterly all-company wellness days where everyone takes a pause together

- Country specific holidays plus a day off for your birthday

- One-time home office stipend

- Annual professional development budget

- Quarterly well-being stipend

- Considerable paid parental leave

- Employee referral bonus program

- Other benefits (life/AD&D, disability, EAP, etc. - varies by country)

About Mozilla 

Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. Join us to work on the Web as the platform and help create more opportunity and innovation for everyone online.

Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging 

Mozilla understands that valuing diverse creative practices and forms of knowledge are crucial to and enrich the company’s core mission. We encourage applications from everyone, including members of all equity-seeking communities, such as (but certainly not limited to) women, racialized and Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, persons of all sexual orientations, gender identities, and expressions.

We will ensure that qualified individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, as appropriate. Please contact us at hiringaccommodation@mozilla.com to request accommodation.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race (including hairstyle and texture), religion (including religious grooming and dress practices), gender, gender identity, gender expression, color, national origin, pregnancy, ancestry, domestic partner status, disability, sexual orientation, age, genetic predisposition, medical condition, marital status, citizenship status, military or veteran status, or any other basis covered by applicable laws. Mozilla will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics or any other unlawful behavior, conduct, or purpose.

title: Engineering Manager
description:
At NetBox Labs , our mission is to make it easier to build and manage complex networks. As a product company, we do that by developing innovative software for network professionals delivered on-premises and in the cloud.

We believe in the power of community and collaboration, and we are looking for a hands-on, player-coach Engineering Manager to lead one of our talented teams. These teams build our core software applications including NetBox and NetBox Add-ons, SDKs, and Plugins, and our observability suite including Diode, Diode Agents and SDKs, and Orb. Much of this development is open source and done in collaboration with our community, but also spans source-available and proprietary software. This role reports to the Director of Engineering.

In this role you will: 

- 
Lead a squad of engineers day-to-day while staying hands-on: reviewing code, jumping into design discussions, and occasionally shipping code yourself to unblock the team or model best practices.

- 
Drive execution relentlessly — break down ambiguous problems into clear plans, set sprint goals, remove blockers fast, and hold the team accountable to deadlines.

- 
Own the software development lifecycle for your team's projects, from planning and design through implementation, testing, and release.

- 
Run effective sprint planning, stand-ups, and retros using GitHub and internal tools, helping engineers break work into well-scoped, executable pieces.

- 
Champion modern, secure software development practices and keep quality bars high without slowing the team down.

- 
Partner closely with product managers to translate customer and community problems into shippable plans, pushing back with data when scope or timelines don't add up.

- 
Coach and mentor engineers individually — give direct, timely feedback, help them grow technically, and build a strong bench for future hiring.

- 
Foster a culture of ownership, continuous improvement, and knowledge sharing within the team.

- 
Act as a liaison between your team and the broader tech community, supporting open-source contributors and guiding community-facing initiatives where relevant.

- 
Report progress transparently to engineering leadership, flagging risks early rather than after they've become problems.

- 
Stay close enough to the code and the architecture to make credible calls on technical trade-offs, while trusting your engineers to own the details of implementation.

You will work closely with: 

- 
Director of Engineering to coordinate cross-functional initiatives and ensure your team's work runs smoothly in our commercial products.

- 
Product team to understand customer and community problems and turn them into a stellar user experience.

- 
Peer engineering managers to plan cross-functional projects, clarify ownership, surface dependencies, and clear blockers together.

Qualifications: 

- 
2+ years of experience as an Engineering Manager or Team Lead, ideally in a player-coach capacity where you're still writing code or reviewing PRs regularly.

- 
A track record of driving projects to completion on tight timelines, with a strong bias toward action and unblocking your team over process for its own sake.

- 
Strong technical background sufficient to review designs and code, and earn credibility with senior engineers.

- 
Experience with Agile methodologies, DevOps, and CI/CD in a fast-moving environment.

- 
Proficiency with GitHub for code management, project tracking, and collaboration.

- 
Solid understanding of software security principles and practices.

- 
Experience with open-source software development and community engagement is a plus.

- 
Excellent, direct communication skills — comfortable giving and receiving fast feedback in a remote, async-first environment.

- 
Proven ability to coach engineers and help them grow, while still being the person who rolls up their sleeves when the team needs it.

It would be fantastic if you have the following background: 

- 
Networking industry experience.

- 
Familiarity with Python, Django, Go, gRPC, or OpenTelemetry.

- 
Knowledge of cloud platforms and services (e.g., AWS, Azure).

- 
Familiarity with containerization and orchestration tools (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes).

- 
Understanding of data privacy regulations and compliance requirements.

About NetBox Labs:

NetBox Labs helps companies build and manage complex networks. We help customers accelerate network automation by delivering open, composable products and supporting the network automation community.

NetBox Labs is the commercial steward of open source NetBox, the world’s most popular network source of truth, and Orb, the next-generation open source network observability platform. Our products include NetBox Enterprise, a fully supported self-managed NetBox with advanced features, and NetBox Cloud, a secure, scalable, and reliable SaaS edition of NetBox.

NetBox powers thousands of companies, and NetBox Labs is backed by investment from Notable Capital (formerly GGV), Grafana Labs CEO Raj Dutt, Flybridge, IBM, Salesforce Ventures, and Mango Capital.

Our culture and values: 

- 
We own and solve problems with high attention to detail.

- 
Our open source contributors, users, customers & team are all part of our community. When our community wins, we win.

- 
We prioritize simplicity and think twice before adding complexity

- 
Clear communication helps keep our team aligned and collaborating smoothly.

NetBox Labs is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe diverse teams build better software, and we welcome applicants of every race, color, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, and veteran status. If you need accommodation at any point in the process, just let us know.

title: Senior Manager, Solution Engineering - DocV
description:
Why Socure ? 

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.

About the Role

title: Chief Technology Officer - US-Based
description:
About Toptal 

Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe , Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce .

We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.

Position Description:

As Chief Technology Officer, you will drive execution for the product and engineering teams and put AI at the core of everything the company builds. You will own Toptal’s full technical architecture and you will build it AI-first—utilizing best practices for agentic engineering. AI is not a workstream inside the engineer team—its core to it.

You will create and own the AI architecture and best practices the rest of the company utilizes. You will also own the initiatives that put agents into production. You should know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up, how to engineer best-in-class harnesses, and how to create best practices for agentic engineering that engineering teams adopt to 10x their productivity—without sacrificing quality. Your mindset will be that of a builder and an architect, someone who solves problems in the system itself. No problem will be too large or too small for you to solve yourself. You will set the technical direction and hold the cadenced meetings that turns technical strategy into working, production-ready outcomes. You will be in the design reviews and in the code, not adjacent to them. You will move fast, and you will ensure our engineering team is never the reason an initiative slows down.

You are the technical owner of all Toptal’s products. You will collaborate closely with Product to design infrastructure that exposes Toptal’s core business logic through modular interfaces the rest of the business can build on. Alongside a group of hands-on executives, your engineering discipline directly shapes Toptal’s growth, profitability, and operational excellence.

You will own resourcing and workforce planning as a doer: scoping the work, sizing the teams, planning headcount against it, defining the role and the bar for every seat. None of that is beneath the role, and we are not interested in someone who thinks these tasks can be done properly by handing it off to HR. Hiring is the highest-leverage work you do, and we want someone who is visibly excited about hiring A-players—with a sense of urgency.

Then, you lead the team. You will set the standards, develop people against those standards, and know exactly who is meeting those standards.

You will be one of Toptal’s foremost experts on AI, and you will stay ahead of a field that never stops moving. You will coach engineers on agentic best practices, show the executive team what is newly possible with the new AI tooling, and push AI into every function at Toptal.

This role runs on high-energy execution and attention to detail. You will bring urgency to every part of it and measure yourself on outcomes. We are not looking for someone to oversee this work. We are looking for someone to drive it and get into the details.

This is a remote position. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.

Responsibilities:

The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills. 

One precondition runs through all of it: you conceive the strategy. You will form your own view of where engineering and AI should go, build the case, and bring the CEO a strategy to react to, not a request for direction.

AI and agentic engineering 

- Own Toptal’s AI technology strategy and the architecture beneath it: model selection and fine-tuning, harness design, orchestration, retrieval, context engineering, tool and MCP integration, guardrails, evaluation, and cost control, exposed as primitives every team composes against.

- Deploy agentic engineering at scale against the work that runs this business: matching, vetting, onboarding, delivery, and internal operations. Own the outcomes those agents are accountable for.

- Make AI quality measurable. Own the evals, the regression suites, and the review loops, so quality here is proven rather than claimed.

- Rebuild how the platform gets built and operated, raising output per engineer through AI-assisted development, review, testing, and operations. Engineers have to want this, not comply with it, and creating that pull is on you.

Team, resourcing, and accountability 

- Decide what a team should look like now that the roles have blurred, where the product manager believes they can design and code, the engineer believes they can do product and design, and the designer believes they can code and do product.

- Own resourcing and workforce planning: scope the roadmap into buildable work, plan headcount and sequence, write the specs, and hit time-sensitive hiring commitments.

- Own the bar for the team: assess talent honestly, develop people against the bar, and hold it as the organization grows.

Platform and execution 

- Own the architecture end to end, from services and data flows to interfaces and system boundaries, and hold the standards that keep it coherent as it grows.

- Own throughput, reliability, and the platform layer beneath them, including the AI-dependent paths where latency, drift, and provider outages are real failure modes. Own build-versus-buy, technical debt, secure-by-design architecture, responsible AI, and the engineering and AI cost structure down to inference and token spend.

In the first week, expect to:

- Learn Toptal’s model and platform architecture, and meet the leaders you will depend on across Engineering, Product, Industries, and Services.

- Establish a direct, working rhythm with the CEO.

In the first month, expect to:

- Assess the engineering function honestly, and assess AI maturity with it: what is really in production, what is measured, what is duplicated, and what should be shut down.

- Assess the team against the bar this role requires, and bring the executive team a strategy no one asked you for.

In the first three months, expect to:

- Be executing your own plan, with a review cadence and clear accountability at every level, and your resourcing plan presented.

- Stand up the shared AI architecture and evals, and put one agentic workflow into production with a baseline and a measured result.

In the first six months, expect to:

- Show business impact from agents in production in at least two core workflows, with the evidence behind it.

- Have the leadership team you need, with the bar visibly raised, and throughput and reliability moving on the paths that matter most.

In the first year, expect to:

- Run an engineering organization recognized inside and outside Toptal as one of the most advanced in the industry, with the pull on AI now coming from engineering.

- Have AI leverage embedded in the architecture and the operating model, not living in a portfolio of pilots, and the team you built delivering against plan.

Qualifications and Job Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field is required, and an advanced degree is strongly preferred.

- 15+ years of progressive engineering leadership, including significant time as a CTO or VP of Engineering, or as a direct report to one at meaningful scale.

- Deep, current, hands-on command of modern AI engineering: foundation models, agentic architectures, harness design, retrieval, context engineering, fine-tuning, and evaluation. You have shipped and operated these in production, and you know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up.

- Agentic systems deployed at scale against real business processes, with measured outcomes on cost, cycle time, quality, or revenue, and a record of retiring what did not work.

- Rigor about evaluation. You can explain precisely how you knew a model, prompt, or agent change was an improvement, and you can show the evidence.

- Command of the economics underneath it: model routing, hosted versus self-hosted, inference capacity, latency and cost budgets, and staying portable across providers.

- Further ahead on AI than the executives around you, able to teach it, and proven at moving an organization to adopt something it was not asking for.

- You create strategy rather than administer it, and you win arguments on evidence rather than authority, including your view on what a team should look like in the age of AI.

- Proven ownership of resourcing and workforce planning, and a hiring track record you can quantify. You have made the hard calls when someone was not clearing the bar.

- Currently hands-on. You read and write code, you can take apart a design document or an eval harness and find the flaw in it, and you command distributed systems, service architecture, data-intensive applications, and cloud infrastructure at scale.

- Experience scaling and modernizing a large existing codebase without stopping the business. You have replaced load-bearing systems in flight, not only built greenfield.

- Experience leading a globally distributed, remote team at a technology or hyper-growth company is required. A high-volume, two-sided marketplace or multi-tenant platform is a significant plus.

- Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.

- Speed, ownership, and quality. You move with urgency, decide without perfect information, and treat everything you deliver as a reflection of yourself.

- You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

Essential Job Functions

- Regularly and reliably attend scheduled virtual team meetings on camera.

- Work independently with minimal supervision.

- Use all required digital collaboration tools.

- Prioritize and self-manage workflows and deadlines.

US FLSA Classification: Full-Time/Exempt

title: Developer Advocate
description:
Who We Are 

Our mission is to make the world programmable. Sight is one of the key ways we understand the world, and soon this will be true for the software we use, too.

We’re building the tools, community, and resources needed to make the world programmable with artificial intelligence. Roboflow simplifies building and using computer vision models. Today, over 1M+ developers, including those from half the Fortune 100, use Roboflow’s machine learning open source and hosted tools. That includes counting cells to accelerate cancer research, improving construction site safety , digitizing floor plans , preserving coral reef populations , guiding drone flight , and much more .

Roboflow is supported by great customers and investors, having raised over 63 million from Y Combinator, Google Ventures, Craft Ventures, Sam Altman, Lachy Groom, amongst other leading software investors.

Roboflowers are passionate builders who value ownership, accountability, and a bias toward action. We're curious, hands-on with new tech, and prefer showing our work over talking about it. Many of us have a founder mindset and thrive in our high-autonomy environment.

What You'll Do 

You’ll be responsible for driving our goals for enabling every developer to build with computer vision. You’re not starting from scratch, over a million developers use Roboflow today. We have the raw materials ready to be molded and scaled by a DevRel leader.

Responsibilities include:

- 
Drive awareness and adoption of Roboflow tools in the developer community

- 
Develop tools and integrations to help make Roboflow easier and better for software developers to use

- 
Build projects that will help improve the bleeding edge of the main Roboflow product

- 
Create demos, applications, and technical content while sharing your progress online and promoting Roboflow on social media (ie X, LinkedIn, Twitch, etc)

- 
Create content to educate, inspire, and equip technical audiences with tools and techniques that make them better at their craft

- 
Work with Product, Engineering, and Design to develop new projects in support of the launch of new features

- 
Write guides, examples, and documentation to make our software more accessible and understandable.

- 
Be an active participant in communities like HN, relevant subreddits, Discord groups, GitHub Issues, and the Roboflow forum.

You may also have or quickly develop ideas for amplifying and expanding our community even more -- and we can’t wait to support those as well.

Who You Are 

- 
4+ years of engineering experience

- 
2 + years of DevRel related experience, preference for products in B2B, AI, cloud, and/or developer tools

- 
Track record of shipping software projects with fast adoption and viral growth, either as part of a previous job or on your own

- 
Technical background that enables you to build fast and learn new things quickly

- 
Translate complex information into engaging and easy-to-understand content, guides, tutorials, examples, and applications

- 
End-to-end content creation skillset across written, video, and social media

- 
Self-starter with the ability to analyze ambiguous situations, develop a plan, execute and iterate

- 
Operate with urgency, build consensus, and lead cross-functional teams.

- 
Customer focus and motivated to become an expert on our industry, customers, product, ecosystem, and competitors.

- 
Active contributor to communities online and/or in-person

- 
Bonus: you currently have an engaged following online and an interest in growing your personal audience

Who You'll Be Working With 

You will directly be working with our Marketing Lead, Open Source Lead, co-founders, Product Engineers, and Product Designers.

We are currently a team of 70 team members located all over the US and Europe. Our team’s backgrounds range from high school whiz kids, former founders of technology companies and fashion lines, world-class engineers, CMOs to CEOs, and have experience scaling businesses to millions in revenue. We want to work with exceptional people with a diverse background. At this early stage, you'll have the ability to work cross-functionally with many members of the team and solve a wide array of problems.

Where You'll Work 

Roboflow is distributed across the US and Europe. We currently have Hubs in New York City and San Francisco with a mindset of opening more offices as we grow. We provide opportunities (like team onsites in different cities ) and resources (like a travel stipend) to work in person with other team members as much as you'd like, while also supporting remote team members. You can work from one of our Hubs, work from home, work at co-working spaces, etc. We want you to work where you work best. Learn more about how we work at Roboflow .

When You'll Work 

We don’t have a particular time-zone preference for this role. We have a flexible schedule that allows you to work collaboratively with other team members and asynchronously when needed.

What You'll Receive 

To determine your salary, we use a number of market and data-driven salary sources. We review all salaries every 6 months to ensure we stay in line with the market.

In addition to our cash compensation, we offer generous perks and benefits. Below are some of the highlights:

- 
$4000/yr Travel Stipend to travel anywhere anytime to work alongside other Roboflowers

- 
$350/mo Productivity stipend to spend on things that make your work environment more productive, like high-speed internet at home or a co-working space

- 
$350/mo AI Tools

- 
$150/mo Team lunch

- 
$500/one time Home office

- 
Cover up to 100% of your health insurance costs for you and your partner or family

- 
Equity in the company so we are all invested in the future of computer vision

Interview Process 

Below is the interview process you can expect for this role. We are all motivated to work with an exceptional team and don't currently have recruiters at Roboflow. You will be speaking directly with our team about what it's like to work and thrive here. We like to work fast at Roboflow, so don't be surprised if all the below conversations happen over a day or two.

Introduction Phase: 

[45m] Meet with hiring manager, Trevor Lynn to assess for overall mindset and skill set

Team Interview Phase: 

[2 x 60m] Meet with the team

[30m] Meet with hiring manager

Use this time to review specifics about the job description and ask questions before the project phase begins.

Project Phase: 

You’ll build a project with Roboflow within a specified amount of time.

We check references and conduct a background check.

Final Interview Stage: 

[60m] Meet with Co-founder & CTO

[60m] Meet with CEO

[30m] Meet with Head of Operations to discuss culture

Note: you are welcome to request additional conversations with anyone you would like to meet and we will accommodate as best we can.

Not sure if this is you? 

We want a diverse, global team, with a broad range of experience and perspectives. Roboflow is an equal opportunity workplace; we welcome people from all backgrounds, communities, and experiences.

If this job sounds great, but you’re not sure if you qualify, apply to our Former Founders role or subscribe to our career newsletter by emailing "Subscribe" to operations@roboflow.com . We carefully consider every application, and will either move forward with you, find another team that might be a better fit, keep in touch for future opportunities, or thank you for your time.

Equal Employment Opportunity 

At Roboflow, we believe great ideas come from everywhere—and everyone. We’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristics.
